definition_zh: 消除；去除；淘汰；（生理）排出；（数学）消元；（化学）消除反应
definition_en: the act or process of removing something unwanted; exclusion from a competition; discharge of waste from the body; (mathematics) the removal of a variable from a system of equations; (chemistry) a reaction in which a group is removed from a molecule
core_image: 一道门槛：把不需要的人或物推到门外，门内留下干净的空间
scene: 实验室里，研究员让水样流过一根吸附柱。In the lab the researcher runs the water sample through an adsorption column, and the report shows the elimination of lead.
sceneCN: 这里 elimination 是「去除、消除」（第 1 个义项：把不需要的物质从某处移除）；句意：研究员让水样流过吸附柱，检测报告显示铅已被去除。图中可辨识物件：吸附柱、水样瓶、检测报告、铅离子示意点。

pos.zh: 消除；去除；淘汰（不可数，指过程；可数时指一次次具体的清除）
（生理）排出；（数学）消元；（化学）消除反应（专业义，常带修饰语）

senses.title: Removal of something unwanted
senses.definition: the act of getting rid of something that is not wanted, especially a substance, problem, or risk
senses.definitionCN: 把不想要的东西清除掉，尤指物质、问题或风险
senses.example: The elimination of lead from petrol greatly improved urban air quality.
senses.exampleCN: 从汽油中去除铅大大改善了城市空气质量。
senses.why: Elimination is the noun of eliminate, from Latin eliminare 'turn out of doors', itself from ex- 'out' + limen 'threshold'. The suffix -ion names the action: something is pushed across the threshold and left outside.
senses.whyCN: elimination 是 eliminate 的名词，源自拉丁语 eliminare“赶出门外”，由 ex-“出”+ limen“门槛”构成。后缀 -ion 命名动作：某物被推过门槛、留在门外。

senses.title: Exclusion from a competition
senses.definition: the removal of a team or player from a tournament or contest because they have lost
senses.definitionCN: 因落败而把队伍或选手从锦标赛或竞赛中除名
senses.example: Their elimination in the group stage surprised every commentator.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小组赛阶段被淘汰，令所有评论员都感到意外。
senses.why: The threshold image transfers to sport: losing pushes you out of the door of the tournament. The word names the exit, not the defeat itself, which is why 'elimination round' is a scheduled stage rather than a single loss.
senses.whyCN: 门槛意象转到体育：输球就是被推出锦标赛的大门。这个词命名的是“出场”，不是失败本身，所以 elimination round 是预设的阶段，而非某一场失利。

senses.title: Defeat that removes a rival
senses.definition: the defeat of an opponent in a way that ends their participation
senses.definitionCN: 以终结对手参赛资格的方式将其击败
senses.example: A single late goal sealed the champion's elimination of the challenger.
senses.exampleCN: 终场前的一个进球让冠军把挑战者淘汰出局。
senses.why: Here the focus shifts from the loser's exit to the winner's action: the victor is the one who closes the door. English commonly uses 'eliminate' transitively for this, and the noun inherits that agent-free viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 这里焦点从输家离场转到赢家的动作：胜者是把门关上的人。英语常用及物的 eliminate 表达此义，名词继承了这个不点明施动者的视角。

senses.title: Discharge of waste from the body
senses.definition: the discharge of waste products from the body, especially through the kidneys, bowel, or lungs
senses.definitionCN: 废物从体内排出，尤指经肾、肠道或肺排出
senses.example: The kidneys control the elimination of urea and excess water.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏控制尿素和多余水分的排出。
senses.why: Physiology keeps the literal 'out' of ex-: waste crosses the body's boundary and is expelled. The word is more clinical than 'excretion' and often appears in fixed pairs such as 'elimination and excretion'.
senses.whyCN: 生理学保留了 ex- 字面的“出”：废物越过身体边界被排出。这个词比 excretion 更偏临床，常出现在 elimination and excretion 这样的固定搭配中。

senses.title: Removal of a variable in algebra
senses.definition: the process of removing one unknown quantity from a system of equations so that the others can be solved
senses.definitionCN: 从方程组中消去一个未知量，以便求解其余未知量
senses.example: Gaussian elimination turns a complex linear system into a triangular one.
senses.exampleCN: 高斯消元把一个复杂的线性方程组化为三角形方程组。
senses.why: The metaphor is exact: the variable is taken out of the equation, just as a person is taken out of the room. Mathematics borrowed the everyday verb and kept its structure — something is removed so that what remains becomes manageable.
senses.whyCN: 比喻很精确：未知量被从方程中“请出去”，正如人被请出房间。数学借用了日常动词并保留其结构——移走一个，剩下的才可处理。

senses.title: Ruling out possibilities by reasoning
senses.definition: the method of rejecting candidate explanations one by one until only the correct one remains
senses.definitionCN: 逐一否定候选解释，直到只剩正确答案的方法
senses.example: By a process of elimination, the detectives identified the only route the thief could have taken.
senses.exampleCN: 通过排除法，侦探确定了窃贼唯一可能走的路线。
senses.why: This is elimination as a reasoning tool: each rejected option leaves the room, and the solution is what stays. The fixed phrase 'process of elimination' signals that the method, not any single removal, is what produces certainty.
senses.whyCN: 这是作为推理工具的 elimination：每个被否定的选项离开房间，留下的是答案。固定说法 process of elimination 表明，带来确定性的正是方法本身，而非某一次排除。

senses.title: Killing or wiping out a person or group
senses.definition: the killing or removal of a person or group, often used as a blunt or euphemistic term
senses.definitionCN: 杀死或清除某人或某群体，常作直白或委婉说法
senses.example: The regime's elimination of its critics drew international condemnation.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权对批评者的清除招致国际谴责。
senses.why: This darker sense extends 'removal' to human lives. Because the verb can mean both 'remove from a list' and 'kill', the noun inherits an ambiguity that context, not grammar, resolves; dictionaries mark this use as euphemistic or intensified.
senses.whyCN: 这个更阴暗的义项把“移除”扩展到人命。由于动词既可指“从名单上删去”又可指“杀死”，名词继承了这种歧义，只能靠语境而非语法消解；词典把此用法标为委婉或强化。

senses.title: A reaction that expels a group from a molecule
senses.titleCN: 消除反应：基团脱离分子
senses.definition: a chemical reaction in which two atoms or groups are removed from adjacent carbons, leaving a double bond
senses.definitionCN: 一种化学反应：相邻碳上的两个原子或基团被移除，形成双键
senses.example: Dehydration of ethanol is a classic elimination reaction producing ethene.
senses.exampleCN: 乙醇脱水是生成乙烯的经典消除反应。
senses.why: Chemistry reuses the threshold image at molecular scale: a small group leaves the molecule, and the space it vacates becomes a new bond. The technical term is fixed as 'elimination reaction', parallel to 'substitution' and 'addition'.
senses.whyCN: 化学在分子尺度重演门槛意象：一个小基团离开分子，它腾出的空间变成新的键。这个术语固定为 elimination reaction，与 substitution、addition 并列。

intro.en: Elimination is a transparent noun built on the verb eliminate plus -ion. Eliminate comes from Latin eliminare 'to turn out of doors', from ex- 'out' and limen 'threshold'. The whole family therefore begins with a door and a boundary, not with 'removal' in the abstract.
intro.cn: elimination 是动词 eliminate 加 -ion 构成的透明名词。eliminate 源自拉丁语 eliminare“赶出门外”，由 ex-“出”和 limen“门槛”组成。因此整个词族起点是一道门、一条边界，而不是抽象的“移除”。

items.en: Latin limen (genitive liminis) meant 'threshold, doorstep'. With ex- 'out' it formed eliminare 'to turn out of doors, expel'. The noun of action eliminatio named the expulsion itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 limen（属格 liminis）意为“门槛、门口”。加 ex-“出”构成 eliminare“赶出门外、驱逐”。动作名词 eliminatio 命名这一驱逐行为。

items.en: Eliminatio appears in Late Latin legal and ecclesiastical writing for expulsion or exclusion. The spelling passed through French into English with the -ion noun suffix intact.
items.cn: eliminatio 见于晚期拉丁语的法律与教会文书中，义为驱逐或排除。该词经法语进入英语，-ion 名词后缀原样保留。

items.en: English eliminate is recorded in the 1560s in the sense 'to expel, turn out'. The medical use for expelling waste from the body appears soon after, keeping the physical 'out' of the prefix.
items.cn: 英语 eliminate 于 16 世纪 60 年代被记录，义为“驱逐、赶出”。不久后出现“把废物排出体外”的医学用法，仍保留前缀字面的“出”。

items.en: In nineteenth-century algebra, elimination became the standard term for removing an unknown from a system of equations; Gauss and others systematized the procedure. The mathematical sense is a deliberate metaphor built on the Latin threshold.
items.cn: 19 世纪代数中，elimination 成为“从方程组消去未知量”的标准术语，高斯等人将其系统化。这个数学义是对拉丁门槛意象的有意借用。

items.en: Modern physiology, chemistry, and sport each fixed their own compounds: elimination of waste, elimination reaction, elimination round. In all of them the core remains the same — something crosses a boundary and does not come back.
items.cn: 现代生理学、化学与体育各自固定了搭配：elimination of waste、elimination reaction、elimination round。它们的核心不变——某物越过边界且不再返回。

items.en: The use of elimination for killing people is attested in political and military prose of the twentieth century. The exact path of this euphemism is uncertain; dictionaries record it as an intensified extension of 'removal'.
items.cn: 用 elimination 指杀害人命，见于 20 世纪的政治与军事文本。这一委婉语的确切扩散过程来源不确定；词典把它记为“移除”的强化延伸。

note.en: The first group separates words that look close but belong to different roots; the second group separates nouns of removal.
note.cn: 第一组区分词形相近但词根不同的词；第二组区分表示“移除”的名词。

entries.definition: to light something up. It comes from lumen 'light', not limen 'threshold'; the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 照亮某物。它来自 lumen“光”，而非 limen“门槛”；相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: happening before the main event. Latin prae- 'before' + limen 'threshold' gives 'before the threshold', a true relative of elimination.
entries.definitionCN: 在主要事件之前发生的。拉丁语 prae-“在前”+ limen“门槛”给出“门槛之前”，是 elimination 的真同源词。

entries.definition: below the level of conscious awareness. Sub- 'under' + limen 'threshold' describes what stays beneath the sill, the opposite direction from elimination.
entries.definitionCN: 低于意识阈值的。sub-“在下”+ limen“门槛”描述留在门槛之下的东西，与 elimination 方向相反。

entries.definition: taking something away from a place. It is the neutral everyday word; elimination usually implies something unwanted and a system or boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某处拿走。它是中性的日常词；elimination 通常暗示对象不受欢迎且涉及系统或边界。

entries.definition: complete destruction of a problem or disease, from Latin radix 'root'. It stresses wiping out at the root, while elimination can be one step in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底根除问题或疾病，源自拉丁语 radix“根”。它强调连根拔除，而 elimination 可以是过程中的一步。

entries.definition: preventing someone from entering or taking part, from Latin claudere 'to shut'. It describes the closed door; elimination describes the person already pushed through it.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某人进入或参与，源自拉丁语 claudere“关闭”。它描述关上的门；elimination 描述已被推出门外的人。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Latin pair ex- + limen, the living suffix -ion, the fixed phrase process of elimination, and the chemistry term elimination reaction.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 ex- + limen 这一对成分、活的 -ion 后缀、固定说法 process of elimination，以及化学术语 elimination reaction。

normal.en: ex- means 'out' and limen means 'threshold': elimination is literally 'out of the door'.
normal.cn: ex- 意为“出”，limen 意为“门槛”：elimination 字面就是“赶出门外”。

normal.en: The noun is just eliminate + -ion, so learning the verb gives you the noun for free.
normal.cn: 名词就是 eliminate + -ion，记住动词就顺带拿到了名词。

normal.en: In sport an elimination round is the door through which losing teams leave the tournament.
normal.cn: 体育里的 elimination round 就是输家离开锦标赛时走的那道门。

normal.en: Process of elimination: each rejected answer leaves the room until one candidate remains.
normal.cn: 排除法：每个被否掉的答案都离开房间，直到只剩一个候选。

normal.en: In chemistry, a small group walks out of the molecule and the empty space becomes a double bond.
normal.cn: 化学里，一个小基团走出分子，空出的位置变成双键。

abstract.en: A threshold you can picture is stronger than the abstract word 'removal' — every sense of elimination is someone or something standing at that door.
abstract.cn: 可画出的门槛比抽象的“移除”更有力——elimination 的每个义项都是某人某物站在那道门前。

abstract.en: Systems clean themselves by expelling: equations, bodies, tournaments and molecules all use the same doorway.
abstract.cn: 系统靠排出保持干净：方程、身体、锦标赛和分子用的是同一道门。

abstract.en: What is eliminated is gone but the boundary remains; the word describes an exit, never an empty space.
abstract.cn: 被消除的东西走了，但边界还在；这个词描述的是出口，而不是空无。

examples.en: The elimination of sulfur from fuel is required before it can be burned cleanly.
examples.cn: 燃料燃烧前必须去除其中的硫。

examples.en: The team's elimination in the semifinal ended a remarkable season.
examples.cn: 球队在半决赛被淘汰，结束了一个非凡的赛季。

examples.en: By a process of elimination, the engineers traced the fault to a single sensor.
examples.cn: 通过排除法，工程师把故障定位到一个传感器上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一离门，内”——一离开门槛，里面的脏东西就被清到门外 → elimination 消除、淘汰

root: e-/ex-（出）+ 拉丁语 limen“门槛”+ -ion（动作名词后缀）；字面义“赶出门外”，核心是“把不需要的移过边界、留在外面”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of elimination move through one doorway: the threshold where waste, rivals, equations, candidates, molecules and people are pushed outside. The word always names the exit, never the state of being gone.
sensesIntro.cn: elimination 的八个义项都经过同一道门：废物、对手、未知量、候选答案、分子和人被推向外面的那道门槛。这个词命名的总是“出场”，而不是“消失后的状态”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold with a door; what is eliminated is on the far side of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道带门的门槛；被消除的东西已在门的另一侧。

branches.en: MATTER AND BODY: unwanted substances and bodily waste both cross a physical boundary and are expelled.
branches.cn: 物质与身体：不需要的物质与体内废物都越过物理边界被排出。

branches.en: COMPETITION: losing pushes a team out, while the winner is the one who closes the door on a rival.
branches.cn: 竞赛：失败把队伍推出门外，而赢家是把对手关在门外的人。

branches.en: METHOD: algebra and logic eliminate by removing one candidate so that the rest becomes solvable.
branches.cn: 方法：代数与逻辑通过移除一个候选，使剩下的部分可解。

branches.en: HUMAN HARM: the same removal verb, applied to people, becomes a blunt or euphemistic term for killing.
branches.cn: 人身伤害：同一个“移除”动词用在人身上，就成了直白或委婉的杀害说法。

branches.en: MOLECULE: a chemical group leaves and the vacated space becomes a new bond — the doorway at atomic scale.
branches.cn: 分子：化学基团离开，腾出的位置成为新键——原子尺度的同一道门。

intro.en: Elimination is transparently eliminate + -ion, and eliminate itself goes back to Latin ex- + limen. The affix set therefore mixes English derivatives, same-root Latin relatives, and look-alikes built on different roots.
intro.cn: elimination 明显是 eliminate + -ion，而 eliminate 又上溯拉丁语 ex- + limen。因此词缀组同时包含英语派生词、同根拉丁亲属，以及建立在不同词根上的形近词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family clusters around limen 'threshold': eliminare 'expel', eliminatio 'expulsion', and praeliminaris 'preliminary'. The unrelated lumen 'light' is the trap that produces illuminate.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族围绕 limen“门槛”：eliminare“驱逐”、eliminatio“逐出”、praeliminaris“初步的”。无关的 lumen“光”则是产生 illuminate 的陷阱。

items.meaning: the act of removing or expelling
items.meaningCN: 消除；淘汰（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The elimination of the error took three weeks.
items.exampleCN: 消除这个错误花了三周。

items.meaning: to remove, expel, or knock out
items.meaningCN: 消除；排除；淘汰（字面“赶出门外”）
items.example: We must eliminate the duplicates before analysis.
items.exampleCN: 分析前我们必须剔除重复项。

items.meaning: one who or that which eliminates
items.meaningCN: 消除者；清除装置（-or 表施动者）
items.example: The eliminator removes stray characters from the feed.
items.exampleCN: 清除器把数据流中的杂散字符去掉。

items.meaningCN: 消除性的；排除的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The drug has an eliminative effect on excess sodium.
items.exampleCN: 这种药对多余的钠有排出的作用。

items.meaningCN: 可消除的；可淘汰的（-able 表可能）
items.example: The fault is eliminable with a simple filter.
items.exampleCN: 这个故障用一个简单滤波器就能消除。

items.meaningCN: 消除的；淘汰性的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The committee took an eliminatory vote.
items.exampleCN: 委员会进行了一次淘汰性表决。

items.meaning: relating to a threshold or boundary
items.meaningCN: 阈限的；门槛的（limen + -al）
items.example: The ritual marks a liminal moment between two states.
items.exampleCN: 这一仪式标记了两种状态之间的阈限时刻。

items.meaningCN: 初步的；预备的（“门槛之前”）
items.example: The preliminary results look promising.
items.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来有希望。

latinEntries.meaning: to turn out of doors, expel

definition_zh: 出现；显现；（新事物的）产生、兴起；（生物）羽化、出土；（哲学）涌现；（从麻醉等状态）苏醒；古义：意外事件
definition_en: the act of coming into view or into existence; the rise of a new phenomenon, group, or idea; (biology) the appearance of an adult insect or a shoot above the surface; (philosophy and complexity science) the arising of properties not predictable from components; recovery from anaesthesia or a similar state; (archaic) an unforeseen event
core_image: 水面下浮起一个形状，先是一团模糊的暗影，然后破出水面，被光看见
scene: 池塘边，孩子指着水面：一只蜻蜓正从水下的幼虫壳里钻出来。By the pond a child points at a dragonfly climbing out of its underwater shell: its emergence.
sceneCN: 这里 emergence 是「羽化、出水」（第 3 个义项：昆虫成虫从蛹壳或水中出来）；句意：池塘边，孩子指着一只正从水下幼虫壳里钻出的蜻蜓：这是它的羽化。图中可辨识物件：池塘、蜻蜓、蜕下的空壳、孩子的手。

pos.zh: 出现；产生；兴起（不可数，指过程；可数时指一次具体的出现）
（生物）羽化、出土；（哲学）涌现；（医学）苏醒（专业义）

forms.label: 复数（多次出现或多种涌现）

senses.title: Coming into view
senses.definition: the act of appearing or becoming visible after being hidden
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏的事物显现、变得可见的动作
senses.example: The emergence of a fin above the water told us a whale was close.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上露出一个鳍，说明鲸就在附近。
senses.why: Emergence is emerge + -ence, and emerge is Latin emergere, from ex- 'out' + mergere 'to sink, dip'. The word pictures something that was under a surface pushing its way out until it can be seen.
senses.whyCN: emergence 是 emerge + -ence，而 emerge 源自拉丁语 emergere，由 ex-“出”+ mergere“下沉、浸没”构成。这个词描绘的是原本在水面下的东西顶出来、直到被看见。

senses.title: Coming into existence
senses.definition: the process by which a new thing, idea, industry, or social form begins to exist
senses.definitionCN: 新事物、观念、产业或社会形态开始存在的过程
senses.example: The emergence of cheap solar power changed the economics of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价太阳能的出现改变了电力的经济格局。
senses.why: Here the surface is historical rather than physical: a new phenomenon rises above the threshold of notice and becomes a fact in the world. English uses 'the emergence of' as a standard frame for tracing origins.
senses.whyCN: 这里的水面是历史性的而非物理的：新现象升到“可被注意”的阈限之上，成为世界中的事实。英语用 the emergence of 作为追溯起源的标准框架。

senses.title: Insect or plant breaking out
senses.definition: the appearance of an adult insect from its pupa or nymph case, or of a shoot above the soil
senses.definitionCN: 成虫从蛹或若虫壳中出现，或幼苗顶出土面
senses.example: The emergence of mayflies happens within a few warm evenings each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 蜉蝣的羽化每年春天集中在几个温暖的傍晚发生。
senses.why: Biology restores the literal image: the insect was enclosed, then it comes out. The technical noun for this is 'emergence', often paired with 'emergence trap' and 'post-emergence' in ecology and agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 生物学恢复了字面意象：昆虫本被包在里面，然后出来。这个专业名词就是 emergence，在生态学与农业中常与 emergence trap、post-emergence 搭配。

senses.title: Recovery from anaesthesia or coma
senses.definition: the return of consciousness after anaesthesia, sedation, or a coma
senses.definitionCN: 麻醉、镇静或昏迷之后意识的恢复
senses.example: The nurse watched for signs of emergence in the recovery room.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在恢复室观察患者苏醒的迹象。
senses.why: Medical usage treats unconsciousness as a medium: the patient is submerged in it and then emerges. The phrase 'emergence from anaesthesia' is fixed in clinical writing and keeps the same ex- + mergere structure.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把无意识视为一种介质：病人浸在其中，然后浮出。emergence from anaesthesia 是临床写作中的固定说法，保留同样的 ex- + mergere 结构。

senses.title: Emergent properties in complex systems
senses.definition: the appearance of collective properties in a system that cannot be predicted from its individual components alone
senses.definitionCN: 系统整体出现无法仅由单个组成部分预测的集体性质
senses.example: Philosophers debate the emergence of consciousness from complex neural networks.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论意识如何从复杂神经网络中涌现。
senses.why: Philosophy extends the 'coming out' image to levels of description: nothing in a single neuron predicts thought, yet thought emerges from the whole. The noun names the level-jump, not any one component.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把“出来”的意象扩展到描述层级：单个神经元里没有任何东西能预测思想，思想却从整体中涌现。这个名词命名的是层级跃迁，而非某个组件。

senses.title: Rise of a group or nation
senses.definition: the rise to prominence or power of a group, class, or country
senses.definitionCN: 某群体、阶层或国家走向显要或掌权
senses.example: The emergence of a middle class reshaped the country's politics.
senses.exampleCN: 中产阶级的崛起重塑了该国的政治。
senses.why: Social history uses emergence for collective actors entering the visible stage of politics. The word avoids saying they were created; it says they came into view and began to count.
senses.whyCN: 社会史用 emergence 描述集体行动者进入政治可见舞台。这个词不说他们被创造出来，而说他们进入视野并开始有分量。

senses.title: A fact becoming public
senses.definition: the point at which previously hidden information becomes known or public
senses.definitionCN: 此前隐藏的信息变得为人所知或公开的时点
senses.example: The emergence of the memo forced the minister to resign.
senses.exampleCN: 备忘录的曝光迫使部长辞职。
senses.why: Journalism borrows the water image for information: facts rise from concealment into the open. The noun marks the moment of visibility, which is why headlines say 'the emergence of new evidence' rather than 'the discovery'.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业把水的意象借给信息：事实从隐藏处浮到明处。这个名词标记可见性的时刻，所以标题说 the emergence of new evidence，而不说 the discovery。

senses.title: An unforeseen event (archaic)
senses.definition: an unexpected happening that requires immediate attention; the older sense from which 'emergency' developed
senses.definitionCN: 需要立即处理的意外事件；emergency 由此旧义发展而来
senses.example: In seventeenth-century prose, an emergence could mean a sudden crisis, not a slow appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪的文本中，an emergence 可指突发的危机，而非缓慢的显现。
senses.why: This sense is historical. The same verb produced two nouns: emergence for the process of coming out, emergency for the urgent event itself. Modern English keeps them apart, and using emergence for a crisis now sounds archaic.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项属于历史用法。同一个动词产生两个名词：emergence 指“出来的过程”，emergency 指紧急事件本身。现代英语把它们分开，如今用 emergence 指危机显得古旧。

intro.en: Emergence is emerge + -ence, from Latin emergere 'to rise out, come forth', built on ex- 'out' and mergere 'to dip, sink'. The same mergere gives merge, submerge and immersion, so the family is really about surfaces and what lies beneath them.
intro.cn: emergence 是 emerge + -ence，源自拉丁语 emergere“升出、显露”，由 ex-“出”和 mergere“浸、沉”构成。同一个 mergere 还给出 merge、submerge、immersion，因此这个词族真正讲的是“表面”与“表面之下”。

items.en: Latin mergere meant 'to dip, plunge, sink'. With ex- 'out' it formed emergere 'to come up out of, rise out of'. The image is physical: something below a liquid surface pushes upward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mergere 意为“浸入、下沉”。加 ex-“出”构成 emergere“从……中升出”。意象是物理的：液体表面之下有东西向上顶。

items.en: The noun emergentia is attested in Late Latin philosophical writing for 'a rising out'. The word reached English through French, with the -ence suffix marking a state or process.
items.cn: 名词 emergentia 见于晚期拉丁语哲学文本，义为“升出”。该词经法语进入英语，-ence 后缀标记状态或过程。

items.en: English emergence is recorded in the 1640s. Early examples often mean an unexpected occurrence, a sense soon taken over by emergency, which was coined from the same verb with -ency.
items.cn: 英语 emergence 记录于 17 世纪 40 年代。早期例子多指意外事件，这一义项很快被同一动词加 -ency 构成的 emergency 接管。

items.en: Entomology and botany fixed emergence for the adult insect leaving its case and the shoot leaving the soil. The date of this technical specialization is approximate but clearly nineteenth-century.
items.cn: 昆虫学与植物学把 emergence 固定为成虫离壳、幼芽出土。这一专业化的确切年代为大致估计，但明确属于 19 世纪。

items.en: In the twentieth century, emergence became a key term in philosophy and complexity science for properties of a whole that its parts do not individually possess. The usage extends the Latin 'rising out' to levels of organization.
items.cn: 20 世纪，emergence 成为哲学与复杂性科学的关键术语，指整体具有而部分单独不具备的性质。这一用法把拉丁语“升出”延伸到组织层级。

items.en: Today the word covers insects, industries, evidence and consciousness. The unifying test is always the same: something was below a surface or below notice, and now it is above it.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖昆虫、产业、证据与意识。统一的检验始终相同：某物原在表面之下或注意阈限之下，现在到了上面。

note.en: The first group separates words built on the same verb but with different prefixes or suffixes; the second group separates ways of describing something new.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一动词但前缀或后缀不同的词；第二组区分描述“新出现”的不同说法。

entries.definition: an urgent, dangerous situation requiring immediate action. It shares emergere with emergence but names the crisis, not the process of appearing.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的危险紧急情况。它与 emergence 共享 emergere，但命名危机本身，而非显现过程。

entries.definition: to combine into one. Latin mergere alone means 'to dip, sink'; without ex- there is no coming out, only going in.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一。单用拉丁语 mergere 意为“浸入、下沉”；没有 ex- 就没有“出来”，只有“进去”。

entries.definition: to put or go under water. Sub- 'under' + mergere is the exact opposite direction from emergence.
entries.definitionCN: 使沉入水中或潜入水下。sub-“在下”+ mergere 与 emergence 方向正好相反。

entries.definition: the fact of being seen or present. It is neutral and static; emergence stresses the process of coming out from hiding.
entries.definitionCN: 被看见或存在的事实。它中性而静态；emergence 强调从隐藏中出来的过程。

entries.definition: movement to a higher position or status. It matches the upward half of emergence but lacks the idea of a concealing surface.
entries.definitionCN: 向更高位置或地位的移动。它对应 emergence 向上的那一半，但缺少“遮蔽表面”的意思。

entries.definition: the arrival of something important, from Latin advenire 'come to'. It is more formal and more final than emergence, which can describe a still-unfolding process.
entries.definitionCN: 重要事物的到来，源自拉丁语 advenire“来到”。它比 emergence 更正式、更带终结感，而 emergence 可描述仍在展开的过程。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Latin pair ex- + mergere, the sibling nouns emergence and emergency, and everyday frames such as the emergence of new industries and emergence from anaesthesia.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 ex- + mergere 这一对成分、同源姊妹名词 emergence 与 emergency，以及 the emergence of new industries、emergence from anaesthesia 等日常框架。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + mergere 'sink': emergence is something sinking upward until it breaks the surface.
normal.cn: ex-“出”+ mergere“沉”：emergence 是某物一路向上、破出水面。

normal.en: Think of a diver coming up: the same verb gives emerge, emerge + -ence, and the opposite submerge.
normal.cn: 想一个潜水员上浮：同一个动词给出 emerge、emerge + -ence，以及反方向的 submerge。

normal.en: The emergence of an industry is a new thing crossing the line of notice, not being manufactured.
normal.cn: 产业的 emergence 是新事物越过“被注意”这条线，而不是被制造出来。

normal.en: A mayfly's emergence is literal: the adult leaves the nymph case and is suddenly visible.
normal.cn: 蜉蝣的 emergence 是字面意义上的：成虫离开若虫壳，突然可见。

normal.en: Emergence and emergency are siblings: one names the coming out, the other the sudden event that demands action.
normal.cn: emergence 与 emergency 是姊妹词：一个命名“出来”，一个命名需要行动的突发事件。

abstract.en: A surface is a promise: whatever is below it can become visible without being created.
abstract.cn: 表面是一种承诺：其下的东西不必被创造也能变得可见。

abstract.en: Emergence is a level-jump, not a sum: the whole shows something the parts never contained.
abstract.cn: 涌现是层级跃迁，不是求和：整体显露出部分从未包含的东西。

abstract.en: What rises into view also rises into consequence — visibility and power often arrive in the same moment.
abstract.cn: 升入视野的东西也升入影响——可见性与权力常常同时到来。

examples.en: The emergence of online learning changed how universities reach students.
examples.cn: 在线学习的出现改变了大学触达学生的方式。

examples.en: Biologists camp by the river to record the annual emergence of mayflies.
examples.cn: 生物学家在河边扎营，记录蜉蝣每年的羽化。

examples.en: The emergence of the secret report triggered a public inquiry.
examples.cn: 这份秘密报告的曝光引发了公开调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一摸紧，死”——一摸水面，紧跟着死寂的暗处冒出东西 → emergence 浮现、出现

root: e-/ex-（出）+ 拉丁语 mergere“浸、沉”+ -ence（状态名词后缀）；字面义“从水下升出”，核心是“原本在表面之下，现到表面之上”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of emergence all describe a crossing from below to above: from under water, under the soil, under anaesthesia, under notice, or under the level of individual parts. The word measures visibility and existence with the same surface metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: emergence 的八个义项都描述一次“由下到上”的越界：从水下、土下、麻醉之下、注意阈限之下，或从个体部分的层级之下。这个词用同一个表面隐喻同时度量“可见”与“存在”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape rising from below a surface until it breaks through and can be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个形状从表面之下升起，直到破面而出、可以被看见。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: a hidden thing or fact crosses the line of notice and becomes seen or public.
branches.cn: 可见性：隐藏的事物或事实越过注意线，变得可见或公开。

branches.en: EXISTENCE AND POWER: a new industry, class, or nation rises into historical consequence.
branches.cn: 存在与权力：新产业、阶层或国家升入历史影响。

branches.en: LIVING SURFACES: an insect leaves its case, a shoot leaves the soil, a patient leaves anaesthesia.
branches.cn: 生命表面：昆虫离壳、幼芽出土、病人脱离麻醉。

branches.en: LEVEL JUMP: collective properties appear that no single component contains.
branches.cn: 层级跃迁：出现任何单个组件都不包含的集体性质。

branches.en: HISTORICAL SENSE: the same verb once named a sudden event, now carried by its sibling emergency.
branches.cn: 历史义：同一动词曾指突发事件，现由姊妹词 emergency 承担。

intro.en: Emergence is a suffix-rich word: emerge + -ence, with the verb itself made of a Latin prefix and root. The set shows how one verb spawns process nouns, adjectives, and a look-alike sibling noun.
intro.cn: emergence 是后缀丰富的词：emerge + -ence，而动词本身由拉丁前缀与词根构成。这组词展示同一个动词如何产生过程名词、形容词，以及一个形近的姊妹名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is mergere 'to sink'. With ex- it yields emergere 'rise out'; with sub- it yields submergere 'sink under'. The noun suffixes -ence and -ency later split into emergence and emergency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 mergere“下沉”。加 ex- 得 emergere“升出”；加 sub- 得 submergere“沉入”。名词后缀 -ence 与 -ency 后来分化出 emergence 与 emergency。

items.meaning: the process of coming out or into existence
items.meaningCN: 出现；涌现（-ence 构成过程名词）
items.example: The emergence of the market took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个市场的形成用了十年。

items.meaning: to come out from below a surface
items.meaningCN: 出现；浮现（字面“从下沉中出来”）
items.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
items.exampleCN: 太阳从云后露出来。

items.meaning: newly appearing; arising as a whole
items.meaningCN: 新出现的；涌现的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: Emergent behavior appears only when many agents interact.
items.exampleCN: 涌现行为只在多个主体互动时才出现。

items.meaningCN: 新兴的；正在形成的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: Emerging economies grew faster than mature ones.
items.exampleCN: 新兴经济体的增长快于成熟经济体。

items.meaning: an urgent situation that suddenly arises
items.meaningCN: 紧急情况（-ency 构成状态名词）
items.example: The hospital declared a public emergency.
items.exampleCN: 医院宣布进入公共紧急状态。

items.meaningCN: 合并（单用 mergere，无“出”前缀）
items.example: The two firms merged last year.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司去年合并。

items.meaning: to put or go under a surface
items.meaningCN: 使沉入；潜入（sub- + mergere）
items.example: The flood submerged the lower fields.
items.exampleCN: 洪水淹没了低处的田地。

items.meaning: the act of coming out of a liquid; rare, chiefly astronomy
items.meaningCN: 出液；复现（罕用，多用于天文）
items.example: The emersion of the star was timed precisely.
items.exampleCN: 这颗星的复现时间被精确记录。

definition_zh: 强调；重点；着重；（语音）重音；（排版）着重标识；（艺术）突出；（音乐）重音；（修辞）强调力度
definition_en: special importance given to something; extra force or stress placed on a word or syllable in speech; typographic marking such as italics or bold; intensity of expression; prominence of form or color in art; the particular focus of a text or discipline; a musical accent; rhetorical insistence
core_image: 一束聚光灯打在一件展品上：周围仍在，但光只让这一件显出来
scene: 演讲者讲到关键处放慢速度，逐个词加重，并在投影上把那一行加粗。The speaker slows down at the key point, weights each word and bolds that line on the screen: that is emphasis.
sceneCN: 这里 emphasis 是「强调、着重」（第 1 个义项：给予某事特别的重要性）；句意：演讲者在关键处放慢速度、逐词加重，并把投影上那一行加粗，这就是强调。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、加粗的那行字、演讲者的手势、聚光效果。

pos.zh: 强调；重点；着重（不可数，常与 on / upon 连用）
（语音）重音；（排版）着重；（艺术、音乐）突出（专业义）

senses.title: Special importance given to something
senses.titleCN: 给予某事物特别重要性
senses.definition: special importance or attention given to a particular point, idea, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 对某一要点、观念或性质给予特别的重要性或关注
senses.example: The report places emphasis on prevention rather than treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把重点放在预防而非治疗上。
senses.why: Emphasis comes from Greek emphasis 'outward show, significance', from en- 'in' + phainein 'to show'. The noun names the act of making one thing stand out so that its importance is visible.
senses.whyCN: emphasis 源自希腊语 emphasis“显现、重要意义”，由 en-“在内”+ phainein“显示”构成。这个名词命名的是让某一点凸显出来、使其重要性可见的动作。

senses.title: Stress on a spoken word or syllable
senses.definition: extra force, length, or pitch given to a word or syllable in speech
senses.definitionCN: 说话时给某个词或音节额外的力度、长度或音高
senses.example: He put the emphasis on 'never', not on 'again'.
senses.exampleCN: 他把重音放在 never 上，而不是 again 上。
senses.why: Speech makes importance audible: the stressed syllable is louder or longer, so the listener hears which part matters. English stress placement can change meaning, as in 'record' the noun versus re'cord the verb.
senses.whyCN: 口语让重要性变得可听：重读音节更响或更长，听者由此听出哪部分重要。英语的重音位置能改变词义，如名词 record 与动词 re'cord。

senses.title: Typographic marking
senses.definition: the use of italics, bold, underlining, or other marks to make words stand out on a page
senses.definitionCN: 用斜体、粗体、下划线等标记让文字在页面上突出
senses.example: The editor added emphasis to the warning by setting it in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把警告设为粗体，以加强强调。
senses.why: Writing replaces the voice with marks: since a page cannot get louder, it changes shape or weight. 'Emphasis' here names the visible cue, and the choice of cue is a matter of house style rather than grammar.
senses.whyCN: 书写用标记代替声音：页面无法变响，就改变形状或粗细。这里的 emphasis 命名可见的提示，而选哪种提示属于体例规范，不是语法问题。

senses.title: Intensity or force of expression
senses.definition: the strength, urgency, or emotional force with which something is said or expressed
senses.definitionCN: 说话或表达时的力度、紧迫感或情感强度
senses.example: She spoke with such emphasis that no one dared interrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时语气如此强烈，没人敢打断。
senses.why: This sense measures force rather than focus. The same Greek root supports 'emphatic' — an emphatic denial is not a highlighted denial but a forceful one, and the boundary between the two senses is often blurred.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项度量的是力度而非焦点。同一希腊词根支持 emphatic——emphatic denial 不是“被标出的否认”，而是“有力的否认”，两个义项的边界常被模糊。

senses.title: Prominence of form or color in art
senses.titleCN: 艺术中形式或色彩的突出
senses.definition: the technique of making a shape, color, or figure stand out against its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 使形状、色彩或人物相对周围环境突出的手法
senses.example: The painter used light and shadow for emphasis on the central figure.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用明暗来突出中心人物。
senses.why: Art criticism borrows the word for visual hierarchy: contrast, placement, and lighting make one element dominant. The metaphor is the same spotlight as in speech, transferred from sound to sight.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评借这个词谈视觉层级：对比、位置与光线使某一元素占主导。隐喻与口语相同，都是一束聚光，只是从听觉转到视觉。

senses.title: Particular focus of a text or field
senses.definition: the aspect of a subject that a text, course, or field chooses to treat as central
senses.definitionCN: 文本、课程或学科选择作为中心来处理的那个方面
senses.example: The course's emphasis shifted from theory to fieldwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课的重点从理论转向了田野工作。
senses.why: Institutions distribute attention: an emphasis is what a syllabus or report decides to make central, with the implication that other things receive less. The phrase 'shift the emphasis' marks this as a movable allocation.
senses.whyCN: 机构在分配注意力：emphasis 是教学大纲或报告决定置于中心的内容，暗示其他方面得到较少关注。shift the emphasis 这一说法表明它是一种可移动的分配。

senses.title: A musical accent
senses.definition: a note or beat given extra stress in a musical phrase
senses.definitionCN: 乐句中给予额外力度的音或拍
senses.example: The conductor asked for more emphasis on the second beat.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥要求第二拍加重。
senses.why: Music transfers the speech stress to rhythm: an accented note stands out the way a stressed syllable does. The underlying metaphor is bodily force, which is why the same word serves voice, print, painting and music.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把语音重音转成节奏：被强调的音像重读音节一样突出。底层隐喻是身体用力，所以同一个词能服务语音、印刷、绘画与音乐。

senses.title: Rhetorical insistence
senses.definition: the deliberate repetition or positioning of words to make an argument or claim land harder
senses.definitionCN: 有意重复或安排词句，使论点或主张更有冲击力
senses.example: The repetition of 'now' gave the closing line its emphasis.
senses.exampleCN: now 一词的重复让结尾句获得了强调力度。
senses.why: Rhetoric studies emphasis as a technique: repetition, short sentences, and contrast all raise the weight of a claim. The Greek origin as 'outward show' fits exactly — the speaker makes the important part appear.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学把 emphasis 当作手法研究：重复、短句与对比都增加主张的分量。希腊词源“向外显现”恰好吻合——说话者让重要的部分“显”出来。

intro.en: Emphasis is a Greek loanword, not an English derivative. Greek emphasis 'appearance, outward show' comes from en- 'in' + phainein 'to show, bring to light', the same verb behind phenomenon and phantom. English added emphasise/emphasize and emphatic on its own soil.
intro.cn: emphasis 是希腊语借词，不是英语派生词。希腊语 emphasis“显现、外观”来自 en-“在内”+ phainein“显示、带到光下”，同一个动词也给出 phenomenon、phantom。英语则在本土另造了 emphasise/emphasize 与 emphatic。

items.en: Greek emphasis meant 'appearance, outward show, significance', from en- 'in' + phainein 'to show'. In rhetoric it named the force that makes a point stand out.
items.cn: 希腊语 emphasis 意为“显现、外观、重要意义”，由 en-“在内”+ phainein“显示”构成。在修辞学中它命名让论点凸显的力量。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as emphasis with the same rhetorical sense. The plural in Latin and in English is emphases, following the Greek -is to -es pattern rather than the English -s.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊名词 emphasis，保留同样的修辞义。拉丁语与英语的复数都是 emphases，遵循希腊语 -is 变 -es 的规则，而非英语加 -s。

items.en: English emphasis appears in the 1570s in rhetorical and grammatical writing. The word entered through Latin and French learned prose, not through everyday speech.
items.cn: 英语 emphasis 于 16 世纪 70 年代出现在修辞与语法著作中。该词经拉丁语与法语学术散文进入英语，而非日常口语。

items.en: The verb emphasize was formed in English in the early eighteenth century by adding -ize to emphasis. Greek had no such verb, so this is a genuinely English creation.
items.cn: 动词 emphasize 于 18 世纪初在英语中由 emphasis 加 -ize 构成。希腊语并无此动词，因此这是地道的英语创造。

items.en: Printing, music, art criticism, and linguistics each adopted emphasis for their own kind of prominence: bold type, an accented beat, a highlighted figure, a stressed syllable.
items.cn: 印刷、音乐、艺术批评与语言学各自采用 emphasis 指其领域的“突出”：粗体、加重拍、被突出的形象、重读音节。

items.en: The plural emphases is fixed. Forms such as 'emphasises' are verb forms, not plurals, which is a common error worth checking in writing.
items.cn: 复数 emphases 已固定。emphasises 这类形式是动词第三人称单数，不是名词复数，这是写作中值得检查的常见错误。

note.en: The first group separates words from the same Greek family with different suffixes; the second group separates nouns of prominence and force.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一希腊词族中后缀不同的词；第二组区分表示“突出”与“力度”的名词。

entries.definition: to give special importance to something. It is an English formation on emphasis, not a Greek verb, and it takes a direct object.
entries.definitionCN: 强调某事。它是以 emphasis 为基础的英语构词，并非希腊动词，且直接带宾语。

entries.definition: forceful and definite in expression. It describes the manner of the expression, while emphasis names the prominence itself.
entries.definitionCN: 表达有力而断然的。它描述表达方式，而 emphasis 命名突出本身。

entries.definition: anything that appears or is observed, from phainein 'to show'. It shares the Greek verb with emphasis but names what shows itself, not the act of stressing.
entries.definitionCN: 任何显现或被观察到的事物，源自 phainein“显示”。它与 emphasis 共享希腊动词，但命名显现之物，而非强调动作。

entries.definition: extra force on a syllable, or pressure on a person or system. In speech it is nearly synonymous with emphasis, but emphasis also covers importance in writing and argument.
entries.definitionCN: 音节的额外力度，或对人、系统的压力。语音上它与 emphasis 几乎同义，但 emphasis 还涵盖书面与论证中的重要性。

entries.definition: a distinctive way of pronouncing, or a musical beat's stress. It is more technical and more local than emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 有特点的发音方式，或音乐拍子的重音。它比 emphasis 更技术化、更局部。

entries.definition: the state of standing out and being noticed. It describes the result; emphasis describes the act of making something stand out.
entries.definitionCN: 突出并被注意的状态。它描述结果；emphasis 描述使某物突出的动作。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Greek pair en- + phainein, the irregular plural emphases, the derived verb emphasize, and fixed phrases such as place emphasis on and with emphasis.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：希腊语 en- + phainein 这一对成分、不规则复数 emphases、派生动词 emphasize，以及 place emphasis on、with emphasis 等固定说法。

normal.en: en- 'in' + phainein 'show': emphasis makes something show forth from the rest.
normal.cn: en-“在内”+ phainein“显示”：emphasis 让某物从其余部分中显现出来。

normal.en: Greek -is becomes -es: one emphasis, two emphases. Never write emphasises as a plural.
normal.cn: 希腊语 -is 变 -es：一个 emphasis，两个 emphases。不要把 emphasises 当复数。

normal.en: Place emphasis on: the preposition is on, because emphasis is weight resting on a point.
normal.cn: place emphasis on：介词用 on，因为 emphasis 是压在某一点上的重量。

normal.en: The verb emphasize was made in English from the noun, so it behaves like a normal -ize verb.
normal.cn: 动词 emphasize 是英语从名词造的，所以按普通 -ize 动词变化。

normal.en: In speech, emphasis is a louder or longer syllable; in print, it is bold or italic; in art, it is contrast.
normal.cn: 口语中 emphasis 是更响或更长的音节；印刷中是粗体或斜体；绘画中是对比。

abstract.en: A spotlight does not add an object; it only decides which object the room is about.
abstract.cn: 聚光灯不增加物体，只决定这个房间“关于”哪件物体。

abstract.en: Attention is a budget: every emphasis quietly defunds something else.
abstract.cn: 注意力是一份预算：每一次强调都在悄悄削减别的项目。

abstract.en: Emphasis is a difference in weight, and weight is only felt against what stays light.
abstract.cn: 强调是一种重量差，而重量只有在与轻的部分对比时才被感觉到。

examples.en: The new curriculum places greater emphasis on critical thinking than on memorization.
examples.cn: 新课程更强调批判性思维，而非记忆。

examples.en: She said 'possibly' with heavy emphasis, making it sound like a warning.
examples.cn: 她重重地说了 possibly，让它听起来像警告。

examples.en: The plural of emphasis is emphases, a detail that many writers get wrong.
examples.cn: emphasis 的复数是 emphases，这是许多写作者会弄错的细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: “俺肥，sis”——俺胖得显眼，妹妹 sis 一眼就看见 → emphasis 显眼、强调

root: 希腊语 en-（在内）+ phainein（显示）+ -sis（动作名词后缀）；字面义“使显现出来”，核心是“让某一点在其余部分中显出来”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of emphasis all perform one operation: raising one element above its neighbours so that it is seen or heard as the point. The medium changes — voice, page, canvas, stage, argument — but the differential remains.
sensesIntro.cn: emphasis 的八个义项都在做同一件事：把某一元素抬到邻项之上，使其被看见或听见为“重点”。媒介会变——嗓音、页面、画布、舞台、论证——但那个“差值”不变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight picking out one object while the rest of the room stays visible but dim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束聚光灯挑出一件物体，其余部分仍在但变暗。

branches.en: ALLOCATED IMPORTANCE: a report or course decides what is central, and the rest receives less attention.
branches.cn: 被分配的重要性：报告或课程决定何为中央，其余得到较少关注。

branches.en: SOUND AND RHYTHM: stressed syllables and accented beats raise one unit above its neighbours in time.
branches.cn: 声音与节奏：重读音节与加重拍在时间中把某一单位抬到邻项之上。

branches.en: SIGHT: bold type and pictorial contrast make the chosen element visible on page or canvas.
branches.cn: 视觉：粗体与画面对比让被选元素在纸面或画布上可见。

branches.en: FORCE: intensity of delivery turns prominence into pressure on the listener.
branches.cn: 力度：表达的强度把“突出”变成对听者的压力。

branches.en: ARGUMENT: repetition and positioning make a claim land harder without adding new content.
branches.cn: 论证：重复与位置让主张更有冲击力，却不增加新内容。

intro.en: Emphasis is a Greek noun that English turned into a verb and two adjectives. The affix set shows the -sis noun, the English -ize verb, the -ic adjective, and the plural rule.
intro.cn: emphasis 是希腊名词，英语把它变成了动词和两个形容词。词缀组展示 -sis 名词、英语 -ize 动词、-ic 形容词，以及复数规则。

latinIntro.en: The Greek family centers on phainein 'to show': emphasis 'outward show', emphatikos 'forceful', and phainomenon 'that which appears'. English added emphasize on its own pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词族围绕 phainein“显示”：emphasis“显现”、emphatikos“有力的”、phainomenon“显现之物”。英语按自身模式加了 emphasize。

items.meaningCN: 强调；重点（-sis 构成动作名词）
items.example: The emphasis falls on the final clause.
items.exampleCN: 重点落在最后一个分句。

items.meaning: to make something stand out as important
items.meaningCN: 强调（英语以 -ize 构成动词）
items.example: The teacher emphasized the main verb.
items.exampleCN: 老师强调了主要动词。

items.meaningCN: 强调的；断然的（-ic 形容词）
items.example: She gave an emphatic 'no'.
items.exampleCN: 她断然说了“不”。

items.meaningCN: 强调地；断然地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He emphatically denied the charge.
items.exampleCN: 他断然否认了指控。

items.meaningCN: emphasis 的复数（-is → -es）
items.example: The two emphases of the plan are cost and speed.
items.exampleCN: 该计划的两个重点是成本与速度。

items.meaningCN: 被强调的（-ed 分词）
items.example: The emphasized phrase appears in bold.
items.exampleCN: 被强调的短语以粗体出现。

items.meaning: too much emphasis on one point
items.meaningCN: 过度强调（over- + emphasis）
items.example: An overemphasis on tests narrows the curriculum.
items.exampleCN: 过度强调考试会窄化课程。

items.meaningCN: 降低强调；去重点（de- + emphasis）
items.example: The redesign led to a de-emphasis of decoration.
items.exampleCN: 重新设计导致装饰被弱化。

definition_zh: 以实证方式；以经验方式；凭观察或数据地；经验主义地；（旧医学）凭经验地；实际上
definition_en: by means of observation, experiment, or experience rather than theory alone; in a way supported by measured data; in the manner of empiricism; (historical medicine) by practical experience without theoretical training; in actual practice
core_image: 一只手把温度计放进烧杯，另一只手在表格上记下读数：先看，再写，不先下结论
scene: 学生把不同浓度的盐水分别加热，记录沸点，再对照理论曲线。The student heats salt solutions of different strength, records the boiling points and compares them with the curve, so the result was obtained empirically.
sceneCN: 这里 empirically 是「以实证方式」（第 1 个义项：通过观察或实验而非纯理论）；句意：学生加热不同浓度的盐水、记录沸点并与曲线对照，所以结论是实证得到的。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、温度计、记录表、理论曲线。

pos.zh: 以实证方式；凭观察、实验或数据地（修饰动词或全句）
经验主义地；（旧医学）凭经验地；实际上（较旧或专业用法）

derivatives.zh: 经验主义者；经验主义的

senses.title: By observation or experiment
senses.definition: in a way based on direct observation, measurement, or experiment rather than on reasoning alone
senses.definitionCN: 以直接观察、测量或实验为依据，而非仅靠推理
senses.example: The hypothesis was tested empirically in three independent laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 该假说在三个独立实验室中接受了实证检验。
senses.why: Empirically is empirical + -ly, and empirical goes back to Greek empeirikos 'experienced', from en- 'in' + peira 'trial, experiment'. The adverb says the route to a claim runs through trial and observation.
senses.whyCN: empirically 是 empirical + -ly，而 empirical 上溯希腊语 empeirikos“有经验的”，由 en-“在内”+ peira“尝试、试验”构成。这个副词说明通往结论的路经过试验与观察。

senses.title: By accumulated experience
senses.definition: on the basis of practical experience accumulated over time rather than formal theory
senses.definitionCN: 依据长期积累的实际经验，而非正式理论
senses.example: Village builders empirically knew which slopes would slide after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的工匠凭经验就知道哪些坡在大雨后会发生滑坡。
senses.why: This sense is older and plainer: knowledge stored in practice. It does not require instruments, only repeated contact with the world and a memory of what followed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项更古老、更朴素：知识储存在实践里。它不需要仪器，只需要反复接触世界并记住随后发生了什么。

senses.title: Supported by measured data
senses.definition: in a manner confirmed by quantitative data rather than anecdote
senses.definitionCN: 以定量数据而非轶事见闻加以确认的方式
senses.example: The effect is empirically small but statistically reliable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个效应在实证上很小，但统计上可靠。
senses.why: Modern research sharpens the adverb toward numbers: 'empirically small' means measured, not merely felt. The contrast is with 'theoretically predicted', which may never be observed at all.
senses.whyCN: 现代研究把这个副词推向数字：empirically small 指“被测出来的小”，而非“感觉上小”。它与 theoretically predicted 相对，后者可能根本未被观察到。

senses.title: In the manner of empiricism
senses.definition: in accordance with the philosophical view that knowledge comes from sensory experience
senses.definitionCN: 依照“知识来自感官经验”这一哲学立场
senses.example: Empirically minded philosophers reject claims that no experience could ever test.
senses.exampleCN: 经验主义取向的哲学家拒斥任何经验都无法检验的主张。
senses.why: Here the adverb labels a philosophy, not a method: it signals that all knowledge claims must answer to experience. The suffix -ly turns the school of thought into a stance toward a question.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个副词标记的是一种哲学而非方法：它表示一切知识主张都必须向经验交代。-ly 把学派变成对某个问题的立场。

senses.title: By practical experience in old medicine
senses.definition: in the manner of the empiric school of ancient medicine, which relied on observed outcomes rather than theory
senses.definitionCN: 按古代医学经验派的作风，依靠观察到的结果而非理论
senses.example: The empiric physicians treated empirically, recording what worked rather than why.
senses.exampleCN: 经验派医生凭经验治疗，记录什么有效，而不是为什么有效。
senses.why: Medical history gives the word a specific ancestry: the Empirici of ancient Greece opposed the dogmatic theorists. 'Empiric' later acquired a negative tinge of 'quack', which is why the adverb's older use needs care.
senses.whyCN: 医学史给了这个词具体出身：古希腊经验派反对教条理论派。empiric 后来带上“江湖医生”的贬义，所以这个副词的旧用法需要小心。

senses.title: As actually found in practice
senses.definition: in actual practice, as opposed to what is supposed or intended
senses.definitionCN: 在实际做法中，而非设想或意图中
senses.example: Empirically, the reform slowed hiring rather than speeding it up.
senses.exampleCN: 实际上，这项改革拖慢了招聘，而不是加快。
senses.why: This use is close to 'in reality'. It reports what happened when the idea met the world, and it often introduces a contrast with official expectations.
senses.whyCN: 这个用法接近 in reality。它报告观念遇到世界后实际发生了什么，常引出与官方预期的对照。

senses.title: By trial and error
senses.definition: by trying different approaches and keeping what works, without a guiding theory
senses.definitionCN: 通过尝试不同做法、保留有效者，而不依赖指导理论
senses.example: They tuned the engine empirically, one setting at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠试错调校发动机，一次改一个设置。
senses.why: Trial and error is the action form of the Greek peira 'trial'. The adverb describes a search without a map: each attempt is a small experiment, and success is remembered.
senses.whyCN: 试错是希腊语 peira“尝试”的动作形态。这个副词描述没有地图的寻找：每次尝试都是一个小实验，成功被记住。

senses.title: In a testable, falsifiable way
senses.titleCN: 以可检验、可证伪的方式
senses.definition: in a form that can be checked against evidence and could, in principle, fail
senses.definitionCN: 以能用证据核查、原则上可能失败的形式
senses.example: Any claim worth making empirically must specify what result would prove it wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 任何值得实证的主张都必须说明什么结果能证明它错。
senses.why: This is the methodological edge of the word: empirical claims expose themselves to refutation. The adverb therefore carries a demand, not just a description — show the test that could go against you.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的方法论锋芒：实证主张把自己暴露给反驳。因此这个副词带着一项要求，而不只是描述——给出可能对你不利的检验。

intro.en: Empirically is a double derivative: empirical + -ly, with empirical from Latin empiricus and Greek empeirikos 'experienced'. Greek peira 'trial' is the seed: the word begins as 'having been tried', not as 'having been believed'.
intro.cn: empirically 是双重派生：empirical + -ly，而 empirical 来自拉丁语 empiricus、希腊语 empeirikos“有经验的”。希腊语 peira“尝试”是种子：这个词起点是“被试验过”，不是“被相信”。

items.en: Greek empeiria meant 'experience', from en- 'in' + peira 'trial, attempt'. Empeirikos described a person guided by experience, especially a physician of the Empiric school.
items.cn: 希腊语 empeiria 意为“经验”，由 en-“在内”+ peira“尝试、试验”构成。empeirikos 形容受经验指导的人，尤指经验派医生。

items.en: Latin empiricus borrowed the Greek adjective and noun, chiefly for the medical sect that trusted observed results over theory. The Latin form is the direct channel to English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 empiricus 借入这个希腊形容词与名词，主要用于信任观察结果而非理论的医学流派。拉丁形式是通往英语的直接通道。

items.en: English empirical first appears in the sixteenth century in medical contexts; by the seventeenth century it extends to any knowledge based on observation. The adverb empirically follows the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 empirical 于 16 世纪首见于医学语境；到 17 世纪扩展到任何基于观察的知识。副词 empirically 随形容词出现。

items.en: The British empiricists gave empirical its modern philosophical weight: all knowledge derives from sensory experience. The adverb then labels that stance as well as the method.
items.cn: 英国经验主义者赋予 empirical 现代哲学分量：一切知识源自感官经验。副词因此既标记方法，也标记这一立场。

items.en: With the rise of controlled experiments and statistics, empirically came to mean 'confirmed by measured data'. The phrase 'empirically supported' became standard in research writing.
items.cn: 随着对照实验与统计学的兴起，empirically 意为“由测量数据确认”。empirically supported 成为研究写作的标准说法。

items.en: The older medical sense survives mainly in histories of science; the everyday modern sense is 'by observation or data'. The negative 'empiric' = 'quack' is a separate, older slang development.
items.cn: 较旧的医学义主要存于科学史；现代日常义是“通过观察或数据”。贬义的 empiric =“江湖医生”是另一条更早的俚语发展。

note.en: The first group separates close forms in the same family and a dangerous look-alike; the second group separates adverbs of evidence and method.
note.cn: 第一组区分同词族的近形词与一个危险的形近词；第二组区分表示证据与方法的副词。

entries.definition: based on observation or experience. It is the adjective that -ly turns into the adverb of manner.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观察或经验的。它是 -ly 转化出方式副词的形容词。

entries.definition: in the manner of an empire, from Latin imperium 'command'. It resembles empirically in sound but has nothing to do with experience.
entries.definitionCN: 以帝国的方式，源自拉丁语 imperium“命令”。它读音近似 empirically，却与经验无关。

entries.definition: a practitioner who relies on experience; historically also a quack. The noun carries a skeptical tone that the adverb does not.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠经验的从业者；历史上也指江湖医生。这个名词带怀疑色彩，而副词没有。

entries.definition: by means of a designed experiment. It stresses controlled procedure, while empirically can include passive observation.
entries.definitionCN: 通过设计好的实验。它强调受控程序，而 empirically 可以包括被动观察。

entries.definition: by watching and recording. It names the act of observation rather than the whole evidential stance.
entries.definitionCN: 通过观看并记录。它命名观察行为，而非整个证据立场。

entries.definition: in practice or almost. It is broader and looser than empirically, which specifically appeals to evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 在实践中，或“几乎”。它比 empirically 更宽泛、更松，后者明确诉诸证据。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Greek peira 'trial', the pair empirical + -ly, the research phrase empirically supported, and the contrast with theoretically.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：希腊语 peira“尝试”、empirical + -ly 这一对、研究说法 empirically supported，以及与 theoretically 的对照。

normal.en: en- 'in' + peira 'trial': empirical knowledge is what has been put into trial.
normal.cn: en-“在内”+ peira“尝试”：经验知识就是被放进试验里的知识。

normal.en: Add -ly to empirical and you get the adverb; the adjective already ends in -al, so the adverb is empirically, not empiricly.
normal.cn: empirical 加 -ly 得副词；形容词已以 -al 结尾，所以是 empirically，不是 empiricly。

normal.en: Empirically supported is the standard phrase in research: support comes from data, not from argument.
normal.cn: empirically supported 是研究中的标准说法：支持来自数据，而非论证。

normal.en: Pair it with theoretically: the two words split a claim into what theory predicts and what measurement shows.
normal.cn: 把它与 theoretically 配对：两个词把主张分成理论预测与测量所见。

normal.en: Trial and error is the everyday shape of empirically: try, watch, keep what works.
normal.cn: 试错是 empirically 的日常形态：尝试、观察、留下有效的。

abstract.en: Experience is a ledger, not a lens: empirically means reading what the world already wrote down.
abstract.cn: 经验是一本账，不是一面透镜：empirically 意味着读世界已经写下的东西。

abstract.en: Every empirical claim carries its own exit: it must name the result that would make it false.
abstract.cn: 每个实证主张都自带出口：它必须说出何种结果会让它不成立。

abstract.en: Data do not shout; empirically is the discipline of listening to small differences.
abstract.cn: 数据不会喊叫；empirically 是听小差异的纪律。

examples.en: The treatment is empirically supported by two large randomized trials.
examples.cn: 该疗法得到两项大型随机试验的实证支持。

examples.en: Empirically, the new schedule reduced waiting times by about ten minutes.
examples.cn: 从实际数据看，新排班把等待时间缩短了约十分钟。

examples.en: Economists disagree theoretically, but empirically the pattern is consistent.
examples.cn: 经济学家在理论上分歧，但在实证上规律是一致的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬皮，离课里”——硬着头皮离开课堂，去现场做试验 → empirically 以实证方式

root: 拉丁语 empiricus / 希腊语 empeirikos（en-“在内”+ peira“尝试”）+ 形容词后缀 -al + 副词后缀 -ly；字面义“凭被试验过的经验”，核心是“靠观察与数据说话”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of empirically share one authority: experience. Whether it is a laboratory measurement, a village craft, a philosophical stance, or a demand for falsifiability, the adverb refuses to let a claim stand on theory alone.
sensesIntro.cn: empirically 的八个义项共享同一个权威：经验。无论是实验室测量、乡村手艺、哲学立场，还是对可证伪性的要求，这个副词都不让主张仅靠理论立足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer in a beaker and a pencil writing down the reading — look first, then claim.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计插在烧杯里，铅笔同时记下读数——先看，再下结论。

branches.en: OBSERVATION AND EXPERIENCE: claims are checked by direct looking or by long practical contact with the world.
branches.cn: 观察与经验：主张靠直接观看或长期实践接触世界来检验。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND REALITY: numbers confirm the effect, and practice reveals what actually happened.
branches.cn: 测量与现实：数字确认效应，实践揭示实际发生了什么。

branches.en: METHOD AND DISCIPLINE: empiricism as a stance demands that any claim expose itself to a possible test.
branches.cn: 方法与纪律：作为立场的经验主义要求任何主张都暴露给可能的检验。

branches.en: MEDICAL ANCESTRY: the Empiric physicians recorded outcomes rather than causes, the word's historical seed.
branches.cn: 医学出身：经验派医生记录结果而非原因，这是该词的历史种子。

branches.en: TRIAL AND ERROR: without a map, each attempt is a small experiment and success is remembered.
branches.cn: 试错：没有地图时，每次尝试都是小实验，成功被记住。

intro.en: Empirically is a clean three-layer derivative: Greek root, Latin adjective, English -al and -ly. The affix set shows each layer and warns against the sound-alike imperially.
intro.cn: empirically 是清晰的三层派生：希腊词根、拉丁形容词、英语 -al 与 -ly。词缀组展示每一层，并提醒防范读音近似的 imperially。

latinIntro.en: Greek peira 'trial' yields empeiria 'experience' and empeirikos 'experienced'; Latin borrowed it as empiricus; English built empirical and then empirically. The unrelated imperium 'command' produces the look-alike imperially.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 peira“尝试”产生 empeiria“经验”与 empeirikos“有经验的”；拉丁语借为 empiricus；英语先造 empirical，再造 empirically。无关的 imperium“命令”产生形近词 imperially。

items.meaning: in a way based on observation or experience
items.meaningCN: 以实证方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The model was empirically calibrated.
items.exampleCN: 该模型经过实证校准。

items.meaningCN: 实证的；经验的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Empirical evidence outweighs speculation.
items.exampleCN: 实证证据胜过猜测。

items.meaning: one who relies on experience; historically a quack
items.meaningCN: 凭经验者；旧指江湖医生
items.example: The empiric trusted outcomes over doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 经验派信任结果而非教条。

items.meaning: the doctrine that knowledge comes from experience
items.meaningCN: 经验主义（-ism 表学说）
items.example: Empiricism shaped British philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 经验主义塑造了英国哲学。

items.meaningCN: 经验主义者（-ist 表人）
items.example: Locke is often read as an empiricist.
items.exampleCN: 洛克常被读作经验主义者。

items.meaning: empirical facts or the empiric school
items.meaningCN: 经验事实；经验派（-s 复数名词）
items.example: The paper collects empirics from ten countries.
items.exampleCN: 论文收集了十国的经验数据。

items.meaningCN: 实证性（-ness 性质名词，罕用）
items.example: The empiricalness of the claim was questioned.
items.exampleCN: 该主张的实证性受到质疑。

items.meaning: treated by empirical methods though not directly observable
items.meaningCN: 准经验的（quasi- + empirical）
items.example: Mathematics has a quasi-empirical side.
items.exampleCN: 数学有准经验的一面。

definition_zh: 使能；使可能；赋能；授权；（教育、残障支持）支持性使能；（计算）启用；（法律）授权；（商业）销售赋能
definition_en: the act of making something possible; the provision of means, authority, or support that allows someone to act; (education and disability) support that removes barriers to participation; (computing) activation of a feature; (law) authorization; (business) the resources and training that let staff perform
core_image: 一把钥匙插进锁孔，门从“锁着”变成“可以打开”——门本身没变，可能性变了
scene: 康复师把助行器调到合适高度，让老人能自己走到窗边。The therapist sets the walker to the right height so the old man can reach the window himself: that is enablement, not carrying him.
sceneCN: 这里 enablement 是「支持性使能」（第 3 个义项：通过支持移除参与障碍）；句意：康复师把助行器调到合适高度，让老人能自己走到窗边；这是支持性使能，不是替他走。图中可辨识物件：助行器、老人、窗边、康复师的手。

pos.zh: 使能；使可能；赋能；授权（多作不可数名词）
（教育、残障、计算、商业）支持性使能、启用、赋能（专业义，常带修饰语）

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多次或多种赋能）

derivatives.zh: 使能者；赋能者；促成因素

senses.title: Making something possible
senses.definition: the act of making something possible that was previously impossible or blocked
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不可能或被阻塞的事情成为可能
senses.example: The new rail link was an enablement of trade between the two valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路线使两个山谷之间的贸易成为可能。
senses.why: Enablement is enable + -ment. Enable is en- 'make, put into' + able, and able goes back to Latin habilis 'easily handled, fit', from habere 'to hold'. The noun names the result: a capacity that was not there before.
senses.whyCN: enablement 是 enable + -ment。enable 由 en-“使、置入”+ able 构成，而 able 上溯拉丁语 habilis“易于处理、合适”，源自 habere“持有”。名词命名结果：此前不存在的能力如今有了。

senses.title: Giving means or authority
senses.definition: the provision of the resources, permission, or authority someone needs in order to act
senses.definitionCN: 提供某人行动所需的资源、许可或权限
senses.example: The grant was an enablement for the clinic to hire two nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款使诊所得以雇用两名护士。
senses.why: Here enablement is something done to a person or institution: means are handed over. The difference from sense 1 is agency — sense 1 is a state becoming possible, sense 2 is an actor being equipped.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 enablement 是对人或机构做的事：手段被交到他们手里。与义项 1 的差别在施动：义项 1 是状态变得可能，义项 2 是行动者被装备起来。

senses.title: Support that removes barriers
senses.titleCN: 移除障碍的支持性使能
senses.definition: support designed to remove barriers so that a person can participate on their own terms
senses.definitionCN: 旨在移除障碍、使人能按自己的方式参与的支持
senses.example: Good enablement in the classroom means changing the task, not lowering the standard.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上良好的支持性使能是调整任务，而不是降低标准。
senses.why: In disability and education policy, enablement is a value word: the aim is the person's own action, not dependence. The support is judged by whether it disappears into the user's capability.
senses.whyCN: 在残障与教育政策中，enablement 是价值词：目标是当事人自己的行动，而非依赖。支持的好坏，看它是否能融入用户的能力之中。

senses.title: Activating a feature in computing
senses.definition: the act of turning on a feature, account, or permission in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统中打开某项功能、账户或权限
senses.example: Enablement of two-factor authentication is now mandatory for staff.
senses.exampleCN: 员工现在必须启用双因素认证。
senses.why: Software narrows the word to a switch: something exists in the system but is off, and enablement turns it on. The noun often appears in rollout documents as a countable process with a checklist.
senses.whyCN: 软件把这个词收窄为一个开关：功能已存在于系统中但处于关闭状态，enablement 把它打开。这个名词常出现在上线文档里，指带清单的可数流程。

senses.title: Legal authorization
senses.definition: the legal power or authorization that allows a person or body to act
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人或机构行动的法律权力或授权
senses.example: The statute's enablement clause allows the agency to set its own fees.
senses.exampleCN: 该法规的授权条款允许机构自行设定收费。
senses.why: Legal drafting uses enablement for the clause that confers power. Without it an act is not merely difficult but ultra vires, so the noun marks a boundary of lawful action rather than a practical aid.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草用 enablement 指授予权力的条款。没有它，行为不只是困难，而是越权，因此这个名词标记的是合法行动的边界，而非实际帮助。

senses.title: Business support for staff performance
senses.definition: the training, content, and tools given to staff, especially sales staff, so they can perform effectively
senses.definitionCN: 为员工（尤指销售）提供的培训、内容与工具，使其能有效工作
senses.example: The company hired an enablement lead to shorten the sales cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘了一名赋能负责人来缩短销售周期。
senses.why: Corporate usage treats enablement as an internal function: it supplies what the front line needs. The word is fashionable and slightly vague, so serious writing usually specifies which enablement — sales, partner, or digital.
senses.whyCN: 企业用法把 enablement 当作内部职能：为一线提供所需。这个词时髦而略空泛，因此严肃写作通常指明是哪一种 enablement——销售、伙伴还是数字化。

senses.title: Capacity building in development
senses.definition: the strengthening of local institutions and skills so that a community can sustain its own development
senses.definitionCN: 增强本地机构与技能，使社区能自行维持发展
senses.example: The programme shifted from delivering aid to enablement of local health teams.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目从直接提供援助转向对本地卫生团队的赋能。
senses.why: Development policy contrasts enablement with provision: instead of giving fish, build the fishing boat and the skills. The noun is thus a theory of aid as capacity transfer, not consumption.
senses.whyCN: 发展政策把 enablement 与直接供给对立：不是给鱼，而是造船与教技能。因此这个名词是一种“援助即能力转移”的理论，而非消费。

senses.title: An enabling condition in philosophy
senses.definition: a condition that makes an outcome possible without by itself causing it
senses.definitionCN: 使结果成为可能、但本身并不导致结果的条件
senses.example: Trust is an enablement condition for any long-term contract.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何长期合同的使能条件。
senses.why: Philosophy distinguishes enabling from causing: a condition may open the door without pushing anyone through it. The suffix -ment turns the verb into a named role in an explanatory structure.
senses.whyCN: 哲学区分“使能”与“致因”：条件可以开门，却不推人过去。-ment 后缀把动词变成解释结构中的一个命名角色。

intro.en: Enablement is enable + -ment, a wholly English formation on an old borrowed adjective. Able comes through Old French from Latin habilis 'fit, easily handled', from habere 'to hold'. The suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum, names the means or result of the action.
intro.cn: enablement 是 enable + -ment，完全在英语中构成，底座是一个借来的古老形容词。able 经古法语来自拉丁语 habilis“合适、易于处理”，源自 habere“持有”。后缀 -ment 来自拉丁语 -mentum，命名动作的手段或结果。

items.en: Latin habilis meant 'easily handled, apt, fit', from habere 'to hold, have'. It described something a person could get a grip on — the physical origin of 'able'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 habilis 意为“易于处理、合适、能干”，源自 habere“持有、抓住”。它形容人抓得住的东西——这是 able 的物理来源。

items.en: Old French took habilis as (h)able, meaning 'fit, capable'. English borrowed it in the fourteenth century, losing the initial h in the modern spelling.
items.cn: 古法语把 habilis 变为 (h)able，义为“合适、有能力”。英语于 14 世纪借入，现代拼写丢掉了词首的 h。

items.en: English enable is recorded in the late fifteenth century, originally 'to make fit or sufficient', then 'to give power or means'. The exact first use is uncertain; dictionaries place it in this period.
items.cn: 英语 enable 记录于 15 世纪晚期，初义“使合适、使充足”，后为“给予权力或手段”。确切首用年代来源不确定；词典把它放在这一时期。

items.en: The noun enablement appears in the seventeenth century in the sense 'the act of enabling'. It remained uncommon in general prose and survived chiefly in legal and institutional writing.
items.cn: 名词 enablement 于 17 世纪出现，义为“使能的行为”。它在一般散文中一直不常见，主要存活于法律与机构文本。

items.en: Computing gave enablement a concrete switch sense, while disability rights and development policy gave it a value sense: support that increases another person's own capacity.
items.cn: 计算给 enablement 一个具体的开关义，而残障权利与发展政策给它一个价值义：增加他人自身能力的支持。

items.en: Sales enablement became a named corporate function in the 2000s–2010s. The term's popularity is recent; its core remains the older idea of supplying means.
items.cn: 销售赋能于 2000–2010 年代成为具名的企业职能。该词流行较晚；核心仍是“提供手段”这一更古老的意思。

note.en: The first group separates words from the enable family and a look-alike with a different root; the second group separates ways of giving power.
note.cn: 第一组区分 enable 词族的词与一个不同词根的形近词；第二组区分“给予能力”的不同说法。

entries.definition: to make possible or give the means. It is the verb that -ment nominalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 使可能或给予手段。它是被 -ment 名词化的动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that enables. The -er suffix marks the source of the capability, while enablement names the act or process.
entries.definitionCN: 使能者；促成因素。-er 后缀标记能力来源，而 enablement 命名行为或过程。

entries.definition: the act of joining the armed forces or a cause, from list 'roll'. It looks like enablement but has no able and no capacity meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 参军或加入某项事业，源自 list“名册”。它形似 enablement，却没有 able，也没有“能力”义。

entries.definition: giving someone power or confidence, especially a group that lacked it. It stresses authority and autonomy more than enablement, which stresses means and possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人权力或信心，尤指原本缺乏的群体。它比 enablement 更强调权威与自主，后者强调手段与可能性。

entries.definition: making a process easier without doing it for the participants. It is procedural; enablement is about capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 让过程更容易，但不替参与者完成。它偏程序；enablement 关乎能力。

entries.definition: the act of making something active or operational. In computing it overlaps sense 4, but it lacks the human-capacity senses.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物活动或运作。计算中它与义项 4 重叠，但缺少“人的能力”诸义。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: en- + able, able from Latin habilis, the suffix -ment, and the modern phrase sales enablement.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：en- + able、able 源自拉丁语 habilis、后缀 -ment，以及现代说法 sales enablement。

normal.en: en- 'make' + able 'capable': enable is literally 'make able', and -ment turns it into the act.
normal.cn: en-“使”+ able“有能力”：enable 字面就是“使有能力”，-ment 把它变成行为。

normal.en: Able comes from habilis 'easy to handle', so enablement originally has a hand-on-a-tool feel.
normal.cn: able 来自 habilis“易于处理”，所以 enablement 最初有“手握住工具”的感觉。

normal.en: Two different jobs: sense 1 opens a possibility, sense 2 hands someone the means. Keep the agent in mind.
normal.cn: 两种不同工作：义项 1 打开可能性，义项 2 把手段交到人手里。要留意施动者。

normal.en: In software, enablement is just a switch; in disability policy, it is a value — support that leaves the user in charge.
normal.cn: 在软件里 enablement 只是开关；在残障政策里它是一种价值——支持之后仍由用户做主。

normal.en: Sales enablement is corporate jargon with an old core: give the front line what it needs to act.
normal.cn: 销售赋能是企业行话，核心很旧：给一线行动所需的东西。

abstract.en: A key does not walk through the door; it only changes what the door permits.
abstract.cn: 钥匙不会穿门而过；它只改变门允许什么。

abstract.en: Real enablement leaves no dependency behind — the support should become invisible in the user's own action.
abstract.cn: 真正的使能不留下依赖——支持应当消失在用户自己的行动里。

abstract.en: Power can be granted or grown: enablement prefers growing, because grown capacity cannot be revoked.
abstract.cn: 权力可以被授予，也可以被生长：enablement 偏爱生长，因为长出来的能力收不回去。

examples.en: The fund's enablement of small clinics allowed them to buy basic diagnostic equipment.
examples.cn: 该基金对小诊所的赋能使其得以购买基本诊断设备。

examples.en: Classroom enablement means removing barriers, not lowering the learning goal.
examples.cn: 课堂支持性使能是移除障碍，而不是降低学习目标。

examples.en: The company invested in sales enablement to shorten the time from lead to contract.
examples.cn: 公司投入销售赋能，以缩短从线索到签约的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一拿不了门特”——一个人拿不动门，特制一把钥匙让他能开 → enablement 使能、赋能

root: en-（使）+ able（有能力的，源自拉丁语 habilis“易于处理”）+ -ment（手段／结果名词后缀）；字面义“使有能力”，核心是“交给你手段，让你自己能做到”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of enablement distribute one idea across very different institutions: a possibility is opened, means are supplied, barriers are removed, a switch is flipped, authority is conferred, staff are equipped, capacity is built, and a condition is named. In every case the actor who benefits is supposed to act.
sensesIntro.cn: enablement 的八个义项把一个观念分布到很不同的机构：打开可能性、提供手段、移除障碍、按下开关、授予权限、装备员工、建设能力、命名条件。每一种情况下，受益的行动者都被期待亲自行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turned in a lock — the door is unchanged, but what it permits has changed.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙在锁孔里转动——门没变，但门允许的事情变了。

branches.en: POSSIBILITY: a blocked outcome becomes possible, or a condition opens the way without causing the result.
branches.cn: 可能性：被阻塞的结果变得可能，或某个条件开路却不导致结果。

branches.en: MEANS AND AUTHORITY: resources are handed over, or a legal clause confers power to act.
branches.cn: 手段与权限：资源被交付，或法律条款授予行动权力。

branches.en: CAPACITY: barriers are removed and local skills are built so that people can sustain their own action.
branches.cn: 能力：移除障碍、建设本地技能，使人能维持自己的行动。

branches.en: SWITCH: an existing feature is turned from off to on inside a system.
branches.cn: 开关：系统内已有的功能从关到开。

branches.en: WORKPLACE: training and tools are supplied so that staff can perform the job they already hold.
branches.cn: 职场：提供培训与工具，让员工能把已有的工作做好。

intro.en: Enablement is a native English construction, so the affix set is mostly English morphology layered on a Latin adjective. It shows the verb, agent noun, participles, and the productive -ment.
intro.cn: enablement 是英语本土构词，因此词缀组主要是在拉丁形容词上叠加英语形态。它展示动词、施动名词、分词，以及能产的 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The Latin seed is habilis 'fit, easy to handle' from habere 'to hold'. English made able, then enable, then enablement; the -ment suffix itself comes from Latin -mentum, a means-or-result noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁种子是 habilis“合适、易于处理”，源自 habere“持有”。英语依次造出 able、enable、enablement；-ment 后缀本身来自拉丁语 -mentum，是表手段或结果的名词词尾。

items.meaning: the act or means of making something possible
items.meaningCN: 使能；赋能（-ment 表手段或结果）
items.example: The enablement of rural clinics took two years.
items.exampleCN: 乡村诊所的赋能用了两年。

items.meaning: to make possible or give the means
items.meaningCN: 使能够；使可能（en- + able）
items.example: The grant enabled the team to continue.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资助使团队得以继续。

items.meaning: a person or thing that enables
items.meaningCN: 使能者；促成因素（-er 表施动者）
items.example: Cheap power was the main enabler of the boom.
items.exampleCN: 廉价电力是繁荣的主要促成因素。

items.meaningCN: 已使能的；已启用的（-ed 分词）
items.example: Enabled devices can join the network.
items.exampleCN: 已启用的设备可以加入网络。

items.meaningCN: 使能的；赋权的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: An enabling environment attracts investment.
items.exampleCN: 有利环境吸引投资。

items.meaning: having the power or skill to do something
items.meaningCN: 有能力的（拉丁 habilis）
items.example: She is able to read three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能读三种语言。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something
items.meaningCN: 能力（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: The ability to focus is trainable.
items.exampleCN: 专注的能力可以训练。

items.meaning: the state of being made unable; a disability
items.meaningCN: 失能；残疾（dis- + able + -ment）
items.example: The injury caused permanent disablement.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤造成永久失能。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 易于处理的；合适的；能干的

definition_zh: 围住；圈占；（被围的）场地、围场；随信附件；圈地运动；（机器）外壳；（生态）围隔实验设施
definition_en: the act of surrounding an area with a fence or wall; an enclosed area of land; something enclosed with a letter or package; the historical conversion of common land into private fields; a casing that surrounds machinery; (ecology) an experimental pen or cage used to isolate a plot
core_image: 一圈栅栏把一块地围起来：里面和外面从此属于不同的规则
scene: 信纸里夹着一张照片，收信人抽出时看到了它。A photograph is folded inside the letter, and the reader pulls out this enclosure.
sceneCN: 这里 enclosure 是「随信附件」（第 3 个义项：与信件一起封入的东西）；句意：信纸里夹着一张照片，收信人把它抽了出来，这就是随信附件。图中可辨识物件：信封、信纸、夹在其中的照片、收信人的手。

pos.zh: 围住；圈占；被围的场地；（信件的）附件（可数／不可数视义项）
（机器）外壳；（生态）围隔设施；（历史）圈地（专业义）

forms.label: 单数（一个围场／一次围住）

derivatives.zh: 关闭；封闭（同源但不同构词）

senses.title: The act of surrounding an area
senses.definition: the act of putting a fence, wall, or barrier around an area
senses.definitionCN: 用篱笆、墙或屏障把一片区域围起来的动作
senses.example: The enclosure of the garden took a week of fencing work.
senses.exampleCN: 把花园围起来花了一周的栅栏活。
senses.why: Enclosure is enclose + -ure. Enclose is en- 'in' + close, and close goes back through Old French to Latin claudere 'to shut'. The suffix -ure names the act or its result, so the word can mean either the fencing or the fenced space.
senses.whyCN: enclosure 是 enclose + -ure。enclose 由 en-“在内”+ close 构成，close 经古法语上溯拉丁语 claudere“关闭”。后缀 -ure 命名行为或其结果，所以这个词既可指“围”的动作，也可指“被围的空间”。

senses.title: An enclosed area of land
senses.definition: a piece of land surrounded by a fence or wall, often used for animals or cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 被篱笆或墙围住的一块地，常用于养动物或耕种
senses.example: The sheep were moved to a smaller enclosure near the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群被赶到谷仓附近一个较小的围场里。
senses.why: The result sense of -ure is at work here: the action of enclosing leaves behind a bounded place. English uses 'enclosure' for pens and paddocks more readily than 'pen', which is smaller and more specific.
senses.whyCN: 这里起作用的是 -ure 的结果义：围的动作留下一个有边界的地方。英语用 enclosure 指围场、牧区，比更小更具体的 pen 更常用。

senses.title: Something enclosed with a letter
senses.definition: an item placed inside an envelope or package along with a letter
senses.definitionCN: 与信件一起放入信封或包裹中的物品
senses.example: Please return the signed form and its enclosure by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前寄回签署的表格及其附件。
senses.why: The physical action becomes a postal convention: whatever is shut inside the envelope is an enclosure. Modern email replaced it with 'attachment', and the older word now sounds formal or legal.
senses.whyCN: 物理动作变成邮政惯例：被封进信封里的东西就是 enclosure。现代电子邮件用 attachment 取代了它，旧词如今显得正式或法律化。

senses.title: The historical enclosure of common land
senses.definition: the conversion of common or open land into privately owned fenced fields, especially in England
senses.definitionCN: 把公地或开放土地转为私有围圈田地，尤指英国
senses.example: The enclosure movement displaced many rural families in the eighteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 18 世纪的圈地运动使许多农村家庭流离失所。
senses.why: History gives the word a heavy social charge: the fence is a legal act that excludes people from land they once used. 'Enclosure movement' is a fixed historical term, and the noun carries dispossession, not just fencing.
senses.whyCN: 历史给这个词沉重的社会含义：栅栏是一种法律行为，把人排除在他们曾使用的土地之外。enclosure movement 是固定历史术语，这个名词承载的是剥夺，而不只是围栏。

senses.title: A casing around machinery
senses.definition: a protective cover or housing that surrounds a machine or its parts
senses.definitionCN: 包围机器或其部件的保护性罩壳
senses.example: The motor's enclosure keeps dust out of the bearings.
senses.exampleCN: 马达的外壳防止灰尘进入轴承。
senses.why: Engineering uses the same 'shut in' structure: the enclosure is the boundary that protects what is inside. Here the purpose flips from excluding people to excluding dust, water, or noise.
senses.whyCN: 工程学沿用同样的“关在里面”结构：外壳是保护内部之物的边界。这里目的从“排除人”转为“排除灰尘、水或噪声”。

senses.title: A pen for farm animals
senses.definition: a fenced structure in which livestock are kept
senses.definitionCN: 用来圈养牲畜的围栏结构
senses.example: The pigs had a shaded enclosure with a wallow at one end.
senses.exampleCN: 猪有一个带遮阴的围栏，一端还有泥浴池。
senses.why: Animal husbandry narrows the land sense to a managed structure with a purpose: feeding, breeding, or protection. The word becomes countable, and 'enclosure' can be temporary or movable.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧用法把土地义收窄为有目的的管理结构：饲喂、繁殖或保护。这个词变得可数，围栏也可以是临时或可移动的。

senses.title: An experimental cage in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的围隔实验设施
senses.definition: a small fenced or caged plot used to isolate organisms under controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 用于在受控条件下隔离生物的小型围圈或网笼样地
senses.example: The researchers compared grazed and ungrazed plots using paired enclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者用成对的围隔样地比较放牧与不放牧的地块。
senses.why: Field ecology turns the enclosure into an instrument: it keeps some things in and others out so that a difference can be measured. The noun here names a treatment, not a possession.
senses.whyCN: 野外生态学把围栏变成仪器：把某些东西留在里面、把另一些挡在外面，从而测量差异。这里这个名词命名的是一种处理，而非占有。

senses.title: A barrier that defines inside and outside
senses.definition: the fence, wall, or hedge itself, considered as the boundary between inside and outside
senses.definitionCN: 作为内外边界的篱笆、墙或树篱本身
senses.example: A high stone enclosure separated the monastery from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一道高高的石围墙把修道院与道路隔开。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the boundary rather than the space it contains. It is the clearest expression of the claudere root: the barrier does not hold anything, it simply decides what is shut out.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项聚焦边界本身，而非它围住的空间。它最清楚地体现 claudere 词根：屏障并不装东西，它只决定什么被关在外面。

intro.en: Enclosure is enclose + -ure. Enclose joins en- 'in' to close, and close descends through Old French clos from Latin claudere 'to shut'. The noun suffix -ure, from Latin -ura, names an act or its result, which is why one word covers both the fencing and the fenced space.
intro.cn: enclosure 是 enclose + -ure。enclose 把 en-“在内”加在 close 上，而 close 经古法语 clos 上溯拉丁语 claudere“关闭”。名词后缀 -ure 来自拉丁语 -ura，命名行为或其结果，所以一个词同时覆盖“围”的动作与“被围的空间”。

items.en: Latin claudere meant 'to shut, close, block'. Its past participle clausus produced clausura 'a closing, a enclosed place', the source of English closure and the model for -ure nouns.
items.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为“关闭、合上、阻塞”。其过去分词 clausus 产生 clausura“关闭、封闭之处”，是英语 closure 的来源，也是 -ure 名词的模板。

items.en: Old French clos 'enclosed, shut' came from clausus. The verb enclore and the noun enclosure developed in French with the sense of shutting something within boundaries.
items.cn: 古法语 clos“被围的、关闭的”来自 clausus。动词 enclore 与名词 enclosure 在法语中发展出“把某物关在边界内”的意思。

items.en: English enclosure is recorded in the fifteenth century for the act of enclosing and for an enclosed place. The variant inclosure was common in earlier modern English and survives in some legal usage.
items.cn: 英语 enclosure 于 15 世纪被记录，指围住的行为与被围的地方。变体 inclosure 在早期现代英语中常见，并在某些法律用法中留存。

items.en: Enclosure became a legal and economic term for converting common fields into private ones. The great English enclosure movement peaked in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
