senses.definition: a statement that two expressions have the same value, or the relation between them
senses.definitionCN: 两个表达式具有相同值的陈述，或它们之间的相等关系
senses.example: The proof relies on an equality between the two integrals.
senses.exampleCN: 证明依赖于两个积分之间的一个等式。
senses.why: Mathematics turns the balance into a symbol: the equals sign asserts that the two sides are level. 'Equality' here is countable — a specific statement, not the abstract principle.
senses.whyCN: 数学把天平变成符号：等号断言两边齐平。这里的 equality 可数——指具体的陈述，而非抽象原则。

senses.title: Equal treatment and fairness
senses.definition: the principle that like cases should be treated alike, without arbitrary difference
senses.definitionCN: 相同情形应相同对待、不得任意区别的原则
senses.example: The policy aims at equality of treatment in hiring and promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 该政策旨在实现招聘与晋升中的待遇平等。
senses.why: This sense adds a normative demand: equality is not just a measurement but a rule about how differences may be used. It is close to fairness, but fairness can allow proportional differences that equality resists.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项加入规范要求：平等不只是测量，而是关于“差异可以被如何使用”的规则。它接近 fairness，但公平可以允许按比例的区别，而平等对此更抵抗。

senses.title: Equality before the law
senses.definition: the principle that the same law applies to everyone and no one is above it
senses.definitionCN: 同一法律适用于所有人、无人凌驾其上的原则
senses.example: Equality before the law is guaranteed by the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 法律面前平等由宪法保障。
senses.why: Law makes the level a civic fact: the scales do not know rank. The phrase is fixed and formal, and it concerns application of rules rather than distribution of resources.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个水平变成公民事实：天平不认等级。这个短语固定而正式，关乎规则的适用，而非资源的分配。

senses.title: Social equality between groups
senses.definition: the condition in which groups have comparable rights, resources, and standing
senses.definitionCN: 各群体拥有可比较的权利、资源与地位的状态
senses.example: Gender equality in pay remains an unmet goal in many industries.
senses.exampleCN: 薪酬上的性别平等在许多行业仍是未实现的目标。
senses.why: Social usage makes equality a measurable gap: the word names a target that can be closer or farther. It often appears with pay, education, and representation, where statistics can show the distance.
senses.whyCN: 社会用法把平等变成可测量的差距：这个词命名一个可以更近或更远的目标。它常与薪酬、教育、代表性搭配，因为统计能显示距离。

senses.title: Equality of opportunity
senses.definition: the condition in which people face the same chances to compete, regardless of background
senses.definitionCN: 不论背景，人们面对相同竞争机会的状态
senses.example: Scholarships were designed to support equality of opportunity rather than equality of outcome.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金的目的是支持机会平等，而非结果平等。
senses.why: This sense distinguishes the starting line from the finish line. Opportunity equality levels the entry conditions; it does not promise that results will be equal, which is why the phrase is politically contested.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项区分起跑线与终点线。机会平等拉平进入条件；它不承诺结果相等，因此这个短语在政治上常有争议。

senses.title: Identity of truth values in logic
senses.definition: the relation between two statements that have the same truth value in every case
senses.definitionCN: 两个陈述在所有情况下真值都相同的关系
senses.example: The two formulas are related by logical equality, not by mere resemblance.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个公式由逻辑等值相联系，而不仅是相似。
senses.why: Logic uses equality for sameness of truth value across all interpretations. It is a stronger claim than 'often alike': two statements can sound different and still be equal in this technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学用 equality 指在所有解释下真值相同。这比“常常相似”强得多：两个陈述可以听起来不同，却在这个专业意义上相等。

intro.en: Equality is equal + -ity, from Latin aequalitas. Equal goes back to aequalis 'even, uniform', from aequus 'level, fair'. The family begins with a physical balance and extends to law, society, mathematics, and logic.
intro.cn: equality 是 equal + -ity，来自拉丁语 aequalitas。equal 上溯 aequalis“平的、均一的”，源自 aequus“平的、公平的”。这个词族从物理平衡出发，延伸到法律、社会、数学与逻辑。

items.en: Latin aequus meant 'level, even, fair'. Aequalis 'uniform, equal' and the noun aequalitas 'equality' were built on it. The root also gives equity, which took the 'fairness' branch rather than the 'sameness' branch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为“平的、均一的、公平的”。在其上构成 aequalis“均等的”与名词 aequalitas“平等”。同一词根还给出 equity，它走的是“公平”分支，而非“相同”分支。

items.en: Old French equalité / égalité carried the Latin noun into medieval usage. English borrowed the form in the fourteenth century as equality, keeping the -ity suffix.
items.cn: 古法语 equalité / égalité 把拉丁名词带入中世纪用法。英语于 14 世纪借入 equality 这一形式，保留 -ity 后缀。

items.en: English equality appears in the fourteenth century with both the mathematical sense 'sameness of quantity' and the social sense 'equal status'. The two branches have coexisted ever since.
items.cn: 英语 equality 于 14 世纪出现，同时带数学义“数量相同”与社会义“地位平等”。此后两条分支一直并存。

items.en: Political writing made equality a claim about rights and government. The exact phrasing shifted over time, but the core demand — no arbitrary rank — remained.
items.cn: 政治写作把 equality 变成关于权利与政府的诉求。具体措辞随时间变化，但核心要求——不得有任意的等级——保持不变。

items.en: Legal equality before the law and social equalities of gender, race, and opportunity became standard phrases. Statistics turned some of them into measurable gaps.
items.cn: 法律面前平等以及性别、种族、机会等社会平等成为标准短语。统计把它们中的一些变成可测量的差距。

items.en: The word now covers equations and civic rights with one image: two sides level on the relevant dimension. The context decides which dimension counts.
items.cn: 这个词如今用一个意象同时覆盖等式与公民权利：两边在相关维度上齐平。由语境决定哪个维度算数。

note.en: The first group separates words from the aequus family with different suffixes; the second group separates equality from neighbouring ideas of fairness and sameness.
note.cn: 第一组区分 aequus 词族中后缀不同的词；第二组区分 equality 与相邻的“公平”“相同”概念。

entries.definition: the same in amount, value, or status. It is the adjective from which equality is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量、价值或地位上相同的。它是构成 equality 的形容词。

entries.definition: fairness, especially in law, from Latin aequitas. Equity adjusts rules to fit cases; equality insists on the same measure for all.
entries.definitionCN: 公平，尤指法律上的公平，源自拉丁语 aequitas。equity 调整规则以适应个案；equality 坚持对所有人用同一尺度。

entries.definition: equality of value or function rather than of amount. It joins aequus to valere 'be worth'.
entries.definitionCN: 价值或功能上的相等，而非数量相等。它把 aequus 与 valere“值”结合。

entries.definition: just treatment according to the case. It can allow differences that equality would reject, so the two words often pull apart in policy debate.
entries.definitionCN: 按情形给予公正对待。它可允许 equality 会拒绝的差异，因此在政策辩论中两词常相互拉扯。

entries.definition: the state of being equal in status or amount, often between countries or currencies. It is more technical and more numerical than equality.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或数量相等的状态，常用于国家或货币之间。它比 equality 更技术化、更数字化。

entries.definition: being exactly alike. It is stronger than equality, which only requires level on one dimension.
entries.definitionCN: 完全相同。它比 equality 强，后者只要求某一维度齐平。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Latin aequus 'level', the pair equal / equality, the opposite inequality, and fixed phrases such as equality of opportunity and equality before the law.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 aequus“平的”、equal / equality 这一对、反义词 inequality，以及 equality of opportunity、equality before the law 等固定短语。

normal.en: aequus means 'level': equality is the state of being on the same line, not being identical.
normal.cn: aequus 意为“平的”：equality 是处在同一条线上，而不是完全相同。

normal.en: equal + -ity: the adjective names the relation, the -ity noun names the state.
normal.cn: equal + -ity：形容词命名关系，-ity 名词命名状态。

normal.en: The equals sign is a tiny balance beam: both sides must weigh the same.
normal.cn: 等号是一台小小的天平：两边必须等重。

normal.en: Equity and equality share a root but differ: equity fits the case, equality fixes the measure.
normal.cn: equity 与 equality 共享词根却有别：equity 适应个案，equality 固定尺度。

normal.en: Equality of opportunity levels the start; equality of outcome levels the finish.
normal.cn: 机会平等拉平起点；结果平等拉平终点。

abstract.en: A level line is not a flat world: equality measures one dimension and leaves others alone.
abstract.cn: 水平线不是平坦世界：平等只测量一个维度，其他维度不动。

abstract.en: Equality is a relation, so it always needs a second term — equal to whom, in what?
abstract.cn: 平等是一种关系，因此总需要第二项——与谁平等，在什么上平等？

abstract.en: The same measure can liberate or ignore: a rule applied to all can be blind to difference.
abstract.cn: 同一尺度既可解放，也可无视：对所有人适用的规则可能看不见差异。

examples.en: The law guarantees equality before the courts for every citizen.
examples.cn: 法律保障每位公民在法庭面前平等。

examples.en: The equation expresses an equality between kinetic and potential energy.
examples.cn: 这个方程表达了动能与势能之间的相等关系。

examples.en: The report measures equality of opportunity across regions rather than equality of income.
examples.cn: 该报告衡量的是地区间的机会平等，而非收入平等。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一夸了提”——一夸就提到人人一样，不能偏心 → equality 平等

root: equal（相等的，拉丁语 aequalis < aequus“平的、公平的”）+ -ity（状态名词后缀）；字面义“处于水平状态”，核心是“在相关维度上齐平”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of equality apply one image — two sides level — to rights, quantities, equations, treatment, law, social groups, opportunities, and truth values. The word never claims identity; it claims parity on a chosen dimension.
sensesIntro.cn: equality 的八个义项把同一个意象——两边齐平——用于权利、数量、方程、待遇、法律、社会群体、机会与真值。这个词从不声称“完全相同”，它声称的是在选定维度上的对等。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance beam that comes to rest horizontal, whatever the two pans contain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平停在同一水平线上，无论两端托盘里装的是什么。

branches.en: MEASURE: people or quantities are placed on a common scale and found level.
branches.cn: 度量：人或数量被放在同一把尺上，并测得齐平。

branches.en: FORMAL SYSTEMS: an equation and a logical equality both assert sameness of value or truth.
branches.cn: 形式系统：等式与逻辑等值都断言价值或真值相同。

branches.en: TREATMENT AND LAW: like cases are treated alike, and no rank stands above the rule.
branches.cn: 待遇与法律：相同情形相同对待，没有等级凌驾于规则之上。

branches.en: SOCIETY: group gaps and starting lines become measurable targets for policy.
branches.cn: 社会：群体差距与起跑线成为可测量的政策目标。

branches.en: RIGHTS: the same status is claimed for all citizens regardless of origin.
branches.cn: 权利：不论出身，所有公民主张相同地位。

intro.en: Equality is a Latin-derived -ity noun on equal. The affix set shows the adjective, verb, adverb, and negative form, plus the same-root but different-branch equity.
intro.cn: equality 是拉丁来源、以 equal 为基础的 -ity 名词。词缀组展示形容词、动词、副词、否定形式，以及同根但走另一分支的 equity。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus 'level' yields aequalis, aequalitas, and aequitas. English takes aequalitas as equality and aequitas as equity, which is why the two words share a root but not a sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus“平的”产生 aequalis、aequalitas 与 aequitas。英语把 aequalitas 取为 equality，把 aequitas 取为 equity，所以两词共享词根却不共享词义。

items.meaningCN: 平等；相等（-ity 表状态）
items.example: Equality before the law is fundamental.
items.exampleCN: 法律面前平等是根本的。

items.meaning: the same in amount, value, or status
items.meaningCN: 相等的；平等的（拉丁 aequalis）
items.example: Two equal parts make a whole.
items.exampleCN: 两个相等的部分构成整体。

items.meaningCN: 使相等；使平等（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The reform aimed to equalize funding.
items.exampleCN: 改革旨在使拨款平等。

items.meaningCN: 同样地；平等地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two options are equally risky.
items.exampleCN: 两个选项风险相同。

items.meaning: the state of not being equal
items.meaningCN: 不平等；不等（in- 否定）
items.example: Income inequality widened last year.
items.exampleCN: 收入不平等去年扩大了。

items.meaningCN: 公平；衡平（同根异义）
items.example: Equity in law can soften strict rules.
items.exampleCN: 法律衡平可以柔化严格规则。

items.meaningCN: 公平的；公正的（-able 形容词）
items.example: An equitable settlement satisfied both sides.
items.exampleCN: 公平的和解让双方满意。

items.meaningCN: 平的；均一的；公平的（拉丁词根）
items.example: The root survives in equal and equity.
items.exampleCN: 该词根存于 equal 与 equity。

definition_zh: 等值；等价；等效；（逻辑）逻辑等值；（数学）等价关系；（化学）当量；（翻译）对等；（学历、资格）等效
definition_en: the state of being equal in value, function, or meaning; (logic) the relation between statements with the same truth value; (mathematics) a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive; (chemistry) the amount of a substance that reacts with one mole of another; (translation studies) the relation between expressions that carry the same meaning across languages
core_image: 两台不同构造的机器输出同一条曲线：外形不同，功能上可以互相替代
scene: 译者把一句中文成语写成英文，读者反应与原句相近。The translator renders a Chinese idiom in English, the readers react as they did to the original, and the class calls this equivalence rather than word-for-word matching.
sceneCN: 这里 equivalence 是「翻译对等」（第 5 个义项：不同语言表达承载相同意义与效果）；句意：译者把中文成语译成英文，读者反应与原句相近，课上把这种关系称为对等，而不是逐字对应。图中可辨识物件：两种文字的稿纸、译者批注、对照箭头、读者反应示意。

pos.zh: 等值；等价；等效（不可数，指关系或状态）
（逻辑）逻辑等值；（数学）等价关系；（化学）当量（专业义，可数）

senses.title: Equality of value
senses.definition: the state of being equal in value, worth, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在价值、意义或重要性上相等
senses.example: The two currencies reached a rough equivalence after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革后两种货币达到了大致等值。
senses.why: Equivalence joins aequus 'level' to valere 'be worth', so its literal sense is 'equal worth'. Unlike equality, it compares value or function rather than status or amount.
senses.whyCN: equivalence 把 aequus“平的”与 valere“值”结合，字面义是“价值相等”。与 equality 不同，它比较价值或功能，而非地位或数量。

senses.title: Equality of function
senses.definition: the condition of being able to perform the same function or role
senses.definitionCN: 能够执行相同功能或角色的状态
senses.example: The two designs achieve functional equivalence with very different parts.
senses.exampleCN: 两种设计用很不同的部件实现了功能等效。
senses.why: The second element of equivalence is valere 'be worth, be strong'. Worth can be measured as what a thing can do, so two different designs that perform the same task are equivalent even when their parts differ.
senses.whyCN: equivalence 的第二个成分是 valere“值、有力”。价值可以按“能做什么”来衡量，所以两个完成同一任务的不同设计，即使部件不同也是等效的。

senses.title: Logical equivalence
senses.definition: the relation between two propositions that have the same truth value in every possible case
senses.definitionCN: 两个命题在所有可能情况下真值都相同的关系
senses.example: De Morgan's laws express a logical equivalence between two forms.
senses.exampleCN: 德摩根定律表达两种形式之间的逻辑等值。
senses.why: Logic makes equivalence exact: not 'similar meaning' but 'same truth value under every interpretation'. This is the strictest version of the word, and it licenses substitution in proofs.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学使等值精确：不是“意义相似”，而是“在每种解释下真值相同”。这是这个词最严格的版本，它允许在证明中替换。

senses.title: An equivalence relation in mathematics
senses.definition: a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, partitioning a set into classes
senses.definitionCN: 具有自反、对称、传递性质，并把集合分成等价类的关系
senses.example: Congruence is an equivalence relation on triangles.
senses.exampleCN: 全等是三角形上的一种等价关系。
senses.why: Mathematics abstracted the everyday idea into three properties: everything is equivalent to itself, if A to B then B to A, and equivalence chains. The result is not one pair but a whole class.
senses.whyCN: 数学把日常观念抽象为三条性质：每物与自身等价、A 与 B 等价则 B 与 A 等价、等价可连锁。结果不是一对，而是整个等价类。

senses.title: Translation equivalence
senses.definition: the relation in which a text in one language produces a meaning or effect comparable to the original
senses.definitionCN: 一种语言的文本产生与原文相当的意义或效果的关系
senses.example: The translator aimed at dynamic equivalence rather than word-for-word fidelity.
senses.exampleCN: 译者追求动态对等，而非逐字忠实。
senses.why: Translation studies uses equivalence for a debated goal: the target text should stand in the same relation to its readers as the source did to its readers. It is a relation between relations, which is why perfect equivalence is rare.
senses.whyCN: 翻译研究用 equivalence 指一个受争议的目标：译文与其读者所处的关系，应像原文与其读者所处的关系。这是“关系之间的关系”，所以完美对等很少见。

senses.title: Equivalence of qualifications
senses.definition: the official recognition that a qualification or standard is comparable to another
senses.definitionCN: 官方承认某一资格或标准与另一者相当
senses.example: The board assessed the equivalence of the foreign degree.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会评估了该外国学位的等效性。
senses.why: Institutional usage makes equivalence a decision, not a measurement: a body declares two credentials comparable. The noun often appears as 'recognition of equivalence', with legal consequences for study or work.
senses.whyCN: 机构用法把 equivalence 变成一个决定，而非测量：某机构宣布两种资历相当。这个名词常以“等效认定”出现，对求学或工作有法律后果。

senses.title: Chemical equivalent amount
senses.definition: the amount of a substance that will combine with or replace one mole of hydrogen or another reference unit
senses.definitionCN: 能与或取代一摩尔氢或其他参照单位结合的物质数量
senses.example: The acid's equivalent weight was used to express its equivalence in the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 该酸的当量被用来表示它在反应中的等价量。
senses.why: Chemistry's 'equivalent' began as the amount that exactly balances another in reaction. The word keeps the balance image but measures reacting power rather than mass alone.
senses.whyCN: 化学的 equivalent 起初指在反应中恰好与另一物平衡的量。这个词保留天平意象，但测量的是反应能力，而不只是质量。

senses.title: Interchangeability in practice
senses.definition: the condition in which two things can be used in place of each other without loss
senses.definitionCN: 两物可以互相替代而不造成损失的状态
senses.example: The manual specifies the equivalence of the two spare parts.
senses.exampleCN: 手册说明这两种备件可以互换。
senses.why: Practical equivalence is the working test of the whole word: if one part can replace the other with no loss of function, the two are equivalent for that job. The abstract relation becomes a maintenance instruction.
senses.whyCN: 实践中的等值是整个词的工作检验：若一个部件能无功能损失地替代另一个，两者在该用途上就是等值的。抽象关系因此变成一条维修说明。

intro.en: Equivalence is equivalent + -ence. Equivalent comes from Latin aequivalere 'be of equal worth', from aequus 'level' and valere 'be worth, be strong'. The word therefore balances two things on the scale of value, not of identity.
intro.cn: equivalence 是 equivalent + -ence。equivalent 来自拉丁语 aequivalere“价值相等”，由 aequus“平的”与 valere“值、有力”构成。因此这个词是在价值的天平上称两物，而不是在“同一性”的天平上。

items.en: Latin valere meant 'be strong, be worth'. With aequus 'level' it formed aequivalere 'to be of equal worth'. The present participle aequivalens named something that balances another in value.
items.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为“有力、值”。加 aequus“平的”构成 aequivalere“价值相等”。现在分词 aequivalens 命名在价值上与另一物平衡的东西。

items.en: Late Latin aequivalentia and French équivalence carried the noun into learned usage. The suffix -ence, from Latin -entia, names a state or relation.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aequivalentia 与法语 équivalence 把名词带入学术用法。后缀 -ence 来自拉丁语 -entia，命名状态或关系。

items.en: English equivalence appears in the sixteenth century in logic and learned prose. Its early work was comparing propositions and translations, not chemicals.
items.cn: 英语 equivalence 于 16 世纪出现在逻辑与学术散文中。早期工作是比较命题与译文，而非化学品。

items.en: Mathematics fixed 'equivalence relation' and 'equivalence class'; chemistry fixed 'equivalent weight'. Both use the word for a balance that permits substitution.
items.cn: 数学固定了 equivalence relation 与 equivalence class；化学固定了 equivalent weight。两者都用这个词表示允许替换的平衡。

items.en: Translation theory adopted equivalence as a central and contested term, distinguishing formal from dynamic equivalence. The debate concerns whether full equivalence is even possible.
items.cn: 翻译理论把 equivalence 采纳为核心而有争议的术语，区分形式对等与动态对等。争论在于完美对等是否可能。

items.en: Today equivalence covers currencies, credentials, spare parts, and logical formulas. The common test is substitution without loss — if one can replace the other, they are equivalent.
items.cn: 今天 equivalence 覆盖货币、资历、备件与逻辑公式。共同的检验是无损失替换——若一者可替代另一者，它们就等值。

note.en: The first group separates same-root words built on aequus and valere; the second group separates equivalence from equality and similarity.
note.cn: 第一组区分建立在 aequus 与 valere 上的同源词；第二组区分 equivalence 与 equality、similarity。

entries.definition: equal in value or function. It is the adjective and noun from which -ence is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 在价值或功能上相等的。它是构成 -ence 的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: in an equivalent way; used in proofs to mark a substitution that preserves truth.
entries.definitionCN: 以等价的方式；在证明中标记保持真值的替换。

entries.definition: sameness of status or amount, from aequalitas. Equality compares levels; equivalence compares worth or function.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或数量的相同，源自 aequalitas。equality 比较水平，equivalence 比较价值或功能。

entries.definition: the state of being alike in some respects. It allows difference; equivalence claims substitutability in the relevant respect.
entries.definitionCN: 在某些方面相似的状态。它允许差异；equivalence 声称在相关方面可替代。

entries.definition: the state of being the very same thing. Equivalence allows two different things to count as the same in value or function.
entries.definitionCN: 是同一事物的状态。equivalence 允许两个不同事物在价值或功能上算作相同。

entries.definition: equality of status or amount, often between currencies. It is more numerical and less functional than equivalence.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或数量相等，常用于货币之间。它比 equivalence 更数字化、更少功能性。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: aequus + valere, the pair equivalent / equivalence, the fixed terms logical equivalence and equivalence relation, and the translation-studies debate.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：aequus + valere、equivalent / equivalence 这一对、固定术语 logical equivalence 与 equivalence relation，以及翻译研究的争论。

normal.en: aequus 'level' + valere 'be worth': equivalence is literally 'equal worth'.
normal.cn: aequus“平的”+ valere“值”：equivalence 字面就是“等值”。

normal.en: Equivalent -> equivalence: drop -ent, add -ence; the noun names the relation.
normal.cn: equivalent → equivalence：去 -ent 加 -ence；名词命名关系。

normal.en: In logic, equivalence means same truth value in every case — substitution is allowed.
normal.cn: 逻辑中 equivalence 意为每种情况下真值相同——允许替换。

normal.en: An equivalence relation has three tests: reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.
normal.cn: 等价关系有三项检验：自反、对称、传递。

normal.en: Translation equivalence is not word-for-word matching; it is matching the reader's relation to the text.
normal.cn: 翻译对等不是逐字对应，而是匹配读者与文本的关系。

abstract.en: Equivalence is a permission to substitute, issued by a chosen scale.
abstract.cn: 等值是一张替换许可，由选定的尺度签发。

abstract.en: Two different things can be equal in worth without ever becoming one thing.
abstract.cn: 两个不同事物可以在价值上相等，却永远不成为同一物。

abstract.en: Every equivalence hides a decision about which differences do not count.
abstract.cn: 每一种等值都隐藏着一个决定：哪些差异不算数。

examples.en: The two methods are logically equivalent but computationally different.
examples.cn: 这两种方法在逻辑上等价，但计算上不同。

examples.en: The committee recognized the equivalence of the two professional qualifications.
examples.cn: 委员会承认了这两项专业资格的等效性。

examples.en: Exact equivalence between languages is rare; translators often settle for functional equivalence.
examples.cn: 语言之间的完全对等很少见；译者常满足于功能对等。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一快，我烂死”——一样快，我就烂死也认它等价 → equivalence 等值、等价

root: aequus（平的）+ valere（值、有力）+ -ence（状态／关系名词后缀）；字面义“价值相等”，核心是“在价值或功能上可以互相替代”。

sensesIntro.en: Equivalence is a relation word: it always compares two things on some scale. Value, function, truth, mathematical structure, meaning across languages, credentials, chemical reacting power, and spare parts are the scales in these eight senses. The constant is substitutability without loss on that scale.
sensesIntro.cn: equivalence 是关系词：它总是在某个尺度上比较两物。价值、功能、真值、数学结构、跨语言意义、资历、化学反应能力、备件，就是这八个义项的尺度。不变的是“在该尺度上可无损失替代”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two differently built machines tracing the same output curve — interchangeable in function, not in form.
core.cn: 核心意象：两台构造不同的机器画出同一条输出曲线——功能可互换，形式不可互换。

branches.en: VALUE AND FUNCTION: worth and role provide the scale on which two different things can balance.
branches.cn: 价值与功能：价值与角色提供了让两个不同事物平衡的尺度。

branches.en: FORMAL SYSTEMS: truth value in logic and structural properties in mathematics make equivalence exact and substitutable.
branches.cn: 形式系统：逻辑中的真值与数学中的结构性质使等价精确且可替换。

branches.en: MEANING AND CREDENTIALS: a translation or a degree is declared equivalent by a community or a board.
branches.cn: 意义与资历：译文或学位由共同体或委员会宣布为对等。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the reacting amount that exactly balances another keeps the oldest scale image.
branches.cn: 化学：恰好与另一物平衡的反应量，保留最古老的尺度意象。

branches.en: PRACTICE: spare parts and systems are equivalent when one can replace the other without loss.
branches.cn: 实践：备件与系统在可无损失替换时是等效的。

intro.en: Equivalence is an -ence noun on equivalent, built from aequus and valere. The affix set shows the adjective, adverb, the noun, and the neighbouring equality, which shares aequus but not the second element.
intro.cn: equivalence 是在 equivalent 上的 -ence 名词，由 aequus 与 valere 构成。词缀组展示形容词、副词、名词，以及共享 aequus 但不共享第二成分的邻居 equality。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequivalere 'be of equal worth' gives aequivalens and aequivalentia. The -ence suffix came through French; the root valere also yields value, valid, and prevail.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequivalere“价值相等”给出 aequivalens 与 aequivalentia。-ence 后缀经法语而来；词根 valere 还产生 value、valid、prevail。

items.meaning: the state of being equal in value or function
items.meaningCN: 等值；等价（-ence 表状态或关系）
items.example: The equivalence of the two methods was proved.
items.exampleCN: 这两种方法的等价性得到了证明。

items.meaning: equal in value, meaning, or function
items.meaningCN: 等值的；等价物（aequus + valere）
items.example: One mile is equivalent to 1.6 kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 一英里相当于 1.6 公里。

items.meaningCN: 等价地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Equivalently, we can reverse the order.
items.exampleCN: 等价地，我们可以颠倒顺序。

items.meaningCN: 等效性（尤指学历，-ency 名词）
items.example: The office issued a statement of equivalency.
items.exampleCN: 该办公室出具了等效证明。

items.meaningCN: 价值（同根 valere）
items.example: The value of the land rose sharply.
items.exampleCN: 这块土地的价值大幅上升。

items.meaningCN: 有效的；正当的（同根 valere）
items.example: The permit is valid for one year.
items.exampleCN: 许可证有效期为一年。

items.meaningCN: 占优势；盛行（prae- + valere）
items.example: Reason prevailed in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 理性在辩论中占了上风。

items.meaningCN: 平等；相等（同 aequus，不同第二成分）
items.example: Equality of pay is still contested.
items.exampleCN: 薪酬平等仍有争议。

definition_zh: 建立；设立；机构；企业；营业场所；（the Establishment）既得权力集团、建制派；证实；（生态）定植；（教会）国教地位
definition_en: the act of setting something up; an organization, business, or institution; the premises of a business; (the Establishment) the established power structure of a society; the proving of a fact; (ecology) the successful settling of a species; the official status of a church
core_image: 一块石头被稳稳放进地基：从这一刻起，它不再移动，别的东西可以依靠它
scene: 记者在报道里写，医学界的既有权威起初并不接受这个发现。The reporter writes that the medical establishment did not accept the finding at first, meaning the existing institutions and authorities.
sceneCN: 这里 establishment 是「既得权力集团、建制派」（第 3 个义项：社会上既有的权力结构）；句意：记者写道，医学建制派起初不接受这个发现，指的是既有机构与权威群体。图中可辨识物件：报道版面、机构徽章、会议桌、记者的笔。

pos.zh: 建立；设立；机构；企业；营业场所（可数／不可数视语境）
（the Establishment）既得权力集团；证实；（生态）定植；（教会）国教地位（专业义）

collocations.phrase: the establishment of a new school

forms.label: 单数（一次建立／一个机构）
复数（多个机构或营业场所）

derivatives.zh: 国教支持者；建制拥护者（罕）

senses.title: The act of setting something up
senses.definition: the act of creating or founding an institution, system, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 创建或创立机构、制度或安排的行为
senses.example: The establishment of the research centre took three years of negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 研究中心的建立花了三年谈判。
senses.why: Establishment is establish + -ment. Establish came from Old French establir, from Latin stabilire 'make stable', built on stabilis 'firm' and stare 'to stand'. The noun names the act of making something stand.
senses.whyCN: establishment 是 establish + -ment。establish 来自古法语 establir，源自拉丁语 stabilire“使稳固”，建立在 stabilis“牢固的”与 stare“站立”上。这个名词命名“使某物站住”的行为。

senses.title: An organization or institution
senses.definition: an organized body such as a school, company, hospital, or government office
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的实体，如学校、公司、医院或政府机关
senses.example: The establishment employs over two hundred staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这家机构雇有两百多名员工。
senses.why: The result of the act becomes a thing: what has been established stands as an institution. This is the most common concrete sense, and it can refer to any organized body, public or private.
senses.whyCN: 行为的结果变成一个事物：被建立起来的东西作为机构而存在。这是最常见的具体义项，可指任何有组织的实体，公私皆可。

senses.title: The established power structure
senses.definition: the powerful groups whose influence is long established, often contrasted with outsiders or reformers
senses.definitionCN: 影响力由来已久的强势群体，常与局外人或改革者对照
senses.example: The proposal was welcomed by scientists but resisted by the political establishment.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案受到科学家欢迎，却遭到政治建制派的抵制。
senses.why: This sense, usually capitalized as 'the Establishment', is twentieth-century British and American usage. It turns 'what is established' into 'who holds power', and it carries a critical tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项通常大写为 the Establishment，是 20 世纪英美用法。它把“被确立的东西”变成“掌握权力的人”，并带批判语气。

senses.title: The premises of a business
senses.definition: a place where a business or service operates, including its buildings and facilities
senses.definitionCN: 企业或服务运营的场所，包括建筑与设施
senses.example: The restaurant is a family establishment with thirty seats.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐馆是只有三十个座位的家庭式营业场所。
senses.why: The concrete result of establishment is a place that stands and operates. The -ment noun turns the act of setting up into the thing set up, so a shop, school, or restaurant is a standing arrangement made visible.
senses.whyCN: establishment 的具体结果是立在那里、持续运营的场所。-ment 名词把“设立”的动作变成“被设立之物”，所以商店、学校或餐馆就是看得见的、站住的安排。

senses.title: The proving of a fact
senses.definition: the act of showing that something is true or certain
senses.definitionCN: 证明某事真实或确定的行为
senses.example: The establishment of the cause took years of forensic work.
senses.exampleCN: 查明并确认原因花了多年法证工作。
senses.why: This sense treats a fact as something that can be made to stand: establishment is giving a claim enough support that it no longer wobbles. The same stability image that describes institutions describes evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把事实当作可以被“立住”的东西：establishment 是给主张足够支撑，使它不再摇晃。描述机构的同一个稳定意象，也用来描述证据。

senses.title: The settling of a species
senses.definition: the successful growth and survival of a plant or animal in a new place
senses.definitionCN: 植物或动物在新地点成功生长并存活
senses.example: Seedling establishment depends on moisture in the first weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗定植取决于最初几周的水分。
senses.why: Ecology uses the word for the moment a species stops arriving and starts holding ground. The same 'stand firm' image applies: a seedling that survives its first weeks is established, and later competition is measured against that stand.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用这个词指物种不再只是到达、而开始占据地面的时刻。同样的“站稳”意象适用：度过最初几周的幼苗就算定植，之后的竞争以这次站住为基准。

senses.title: Official status of a church
senses.definition: the recognition of a church by the state as the official religion
senses.definitionCN: 国家承认某教会为官方宗教
senses.example: The establishment of the church was disputed for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 该教会的国教地位争议了数百年。
senses.why: Here establishment is legal standing conferred by the state: the church is set up as official, with privileges and duties fixed by law. The word names an institutional status, not a building.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 establishment 是国家授予的法律地位：该教会作为官方宗教被确立，特权与义务由法律规定。这个词命名机构地位，而非建筑。

senses.title: A settled household or position
senses.titleCN: 安定的家庭或地位（较旧）
senses.definition: a household, residence, or permanent position, especially in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、住所或永久职位，尤见于较旧用法
senses.example: He kept a modest establishment in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乡下维持着一处简朴的住所。
senses.why: Older usage extends establishment to a settled way of living: a household with its routines and staff. It is the domestic version of 'what has been set up and stands', now largely literary.
senses.whyCN: 较旧用法把 establishment 扩展到安定的生活方式：有常规与人手的家庭。这是“被设立并站住之物”的家庭版本，如今主要见于文学语体。

intro.en: Establishment is establish + -ment. Establish came into English from Old French establir, from Latin stabilire 'to make stable', from stabilis 'firm' and stare 'to stand'. The whole family is about standing firm long enough to be relied on.
intro.cn: establishment 是 establish + -ment。establish 从古法语 establir 进入英语，源自拉丁语 stabilire“使稳固”，再上溯 stabilis“牢固的”与 stare“站立”。整个词族都与“站稳到足以被依靠”有关。

items.en: Latin stare meant 'to stand'. Stabilis 'firm, standing' and stabilire 'to make firm' were built on it, giving the image of something set upright and steady.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为“站立”。在其上构成 stabilis“牢固的、站立的”与 stabilire“使牢固”，给出某物被立直、稳住意象。

items.en: Old French establir 'to set up, found' carried the Latin verb into medieval French. Its noun establissement named the act and the resulting institution.
items.cn: 古法语 establir“设立、创建”把拉丁动词带入中世纪法语。其名词 establissement 命名行为与由此产生的机构。

items.en: English establishment appears in the fifteenth century, first as the act of founding, then as the thing founded. The exact first use is uncertain; dictionaries place it in this period.
items.cn: 英语 establishment 于 15 世纪出现，先指创立行为，后指被创立之物。确切首用年代为大致估计。

items.en: The sense 'household, place of business' developed in ordinary prose, while the church sense became fixed in legal and political argument about state religion.
items.cn: “家庭、营业场所”义在日常散文中发展，而教会义在关于国教的成文法与政治争论中固定下来。

items.en: The capitalized sense for a society's power structure is usually traced to British journalism in the 1950s. The exact coining is uncertain, but the usage spread quickly in both Britain and the United States.
items.cn: 大写义指社会权力结构，通常追溯到 1950 年代的英国新闻写作。确切造词来源不确定，但这一用法在英美迅速传播。

items.en: Ecology fixed 'establishment' for the successful settling of a species, and medicine uses it for the confirmed presence of a diagnosis or condition.
items.cn: 生态学固定 establishment 指物种成功定植，医学用它指诊断或状况被确认存在。

note.en: The first group separates words built on the stare family; the second group separates institutions from neighbouring ideas of organization and foundation.
note.cn: 第一组区分建立在 stare 词族上的词；第二组区分 institution 与相邻的“组织”“基础”概念。

entries.definition: to set up, settle, or prove. It is the verb that -ment nominalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 设立、使安定或证实。它是被 -ment 名词化的动词。

entries.definition: long in place and accepted. It describes the state after establishment, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 确立已久的；公认的。它描述建立之后的状态，而非行为。

entries.definition: firm and not likely to move, from Latin stabilis. It is the adjective behind the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 牢固而不易移动的，源自拉丁语 stabilis。它是整个词族背后的形容词。

entries.definition: an established organization or practice. It overlaps sense 2 but stresses rules and continuity rather than the act of founding.
entries.definitionCN: 已确立的组织或做法。它与义项 2 重叠，但强调规则与延续性，而非创立行为。

entries.definition: the base on which something is built, or an endowed organization. It comes from Latin fundus 'bottom', not from stare.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物所依据的基础，或捐助设立的机构。它来自拉丁语 fundus“底部”，而非 stare。

entries.definition: a commercial business. It is narrower than establishment, which can be a school, a hospital, or a shop.
entries.definitionCN: 商业企业。它比 establishment 窄，后者可以是学校、医院或商店。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Latin stare 'stand', the pair establish / establishment, the fixed phrase the Establishment, and the ecological sense of species establishment.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 stare“站立”、establish / establishment 这一对、固定说法 the Establishment，以及物种定植的生态义。

normal.en: stare means 'stand': establish is to make something stand, and -ment is the standing thing.
normal.cn: stare 意为“站立”：establish 是使某物站住，-ment 是站住的东西。

normal.en: Establish + -ment: the noun covers both the act of founding and the institution founded.
normal.cn: establish + -ment：名词同时覆盖创立行为与被创立的机构。

normal.en: The Establishment is 'what stands' turned into 'who stands' — the people whose position is already secure.
normal.cn: the Establishment 是“站住的东西”变成“站住的人”——地位已然稳固的那群人。

normal.en: A business establishment is a place that stands and operates; a school establishment is the school itself.
normal.cn: 营业场所是立在那里运营的地方；学校 establishment 就是学校本身。

normal.en: In ecology, establishment is the moment a seedling stops being a seed and starts holding ground.
normal.cn: 生态学中，establishment 是幼苗不再只是种子、开始占据地面的一刻。

abstract.en: To establish is to make something stand without being held; stability is borrowed strength becoming its own.
abstract.cn: 建立就是让某物无需扶持也能站住；稳定是借来的力量变成自己的力量。

abstract.en: Institutions are frozen decisions: what was once done repeatedly now stands as a rule.
abstract.cn: 机构是冻结的决定：曾反复做的事，如今作为规则站住。

abstract.en: The Establishment is stability seen from outside — from there, standing looks like power.
abstract.cn: 建制派是从外部看到的稳定——在外部看来，站住就是权力。

examples.en: The establishment of the agency followed years of public pressure.
examples.cn: 该机构的设立是在多年公众压力之后。

examples.en: The proposal was blocked by the financial establishment.
examples.cn: 该提案被金融建制派阻挠。

examples.en: Seedling establishment is highest in the first two weeks after sowing.
examples.cn: 幼苗定植在播种后前两周最高。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一斯台，不立市门特”——一座讲台不立稳，市门口的特权就站不住 → establishment 建立、机构

root: establish（建立，古法语 establir < 拉丁语 stabilire“使稳固”< stabilis“牢固的”< stare“站立”）+ -ment（行为／结果名词后缀）；字面义“使站稳”，核心是“把某物立起来并让它持续存在”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of establishment move from an act to its result and then to its social consequences: founding, the founded institution, the power that comes from being long founded, premises, proof, a species holding ground, a church's official status, and a settled household. All of them rest on the image of standing.
sensesIntro.cn: establishment 的八个义项从行为走到结果，再走到社会后果：创立、被创立的机构、因长期存在而获得的权力、营业场所、证实、物种占据地面、教会的官方地位、安定的家庭。它们都建立在“站立”的意象上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foundation stone set level and firm, so that everything above it can stop moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块地基石被放平、稳住，使上面的一切可以停止移动。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: founding makes something stand, and what stands becomes an organized body.
branches.cn: 行为与结果：创立使某物站住，站住的东西成为有组织的实体。

branches.en: POWER: long standing converts into social influence, seen from outside as 'the Establishment'.
branches.cn: 权力：长期站立转化为社会影响，从外部看就是“建制派”。

branches.en: PLACES: a business or household is a standing arrangement with premises and routines.
branches.cn: 场所：企业或家庭是一种站住的安排，有场所与常规。

branches.en: CONFIRMATION: a fact or a species is established when it can be shown to hold.
branches.cn: 确认：事实或物种被确立，是当它能被证明站得住时。

branches.en: OFFICIAL STATUS: a church is established when the state gives it standing by law.
branches.cn: 官方地位：当国家依法给予某教会地位时，它就是国教。

intro.en: Establishment is a transparent -ment noun on establish, with Latin stabilis and stare beneath it. The affix set shows the verb, participles, the adjective stable, and the key contrast with foundation, which has a different root.
intro.cn: establishment 是在 establish 上的透明 -ment 名词，底下是拉丁语 stabilis 与 stare。词缀组展示动词、分词、形容词 stable，以及与不同词根的 foundation 的关键对照。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'stand' gives stabilis 'firm' and stabilire 'make firm'; Old French establir gives English establish. The -ment suffix, from Latin -mentum, names the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare“站立”给出 stabilis“牢固”与 stabilire“使牢固”；古法语 establir 给出英语 establish。-ment 后缀来自拉丁语 -mentum，命名行为或其结果。

items.meaning: the act of founding or the institution founded
items.meaningCN: 建立；机构（-ment 表行为或结果）
items.example: The establishment of the fund took a year.
items.exampleCN: 该基金的设立用了一年。

items.meaning: to set up, make firm, prove
items.meaningCN: 建立；确立；证实（源自“使稳固”）
items.example: They established a new clinic.
items.exampleCN: 他们建立了一家新诊所。

items.meaningCN: 既有的；确立的（-ed 分词）
items.example: It is an established practice.
items.exampleCN: 这是既定做法。

items.meaning: in the process of being founded
items.meaningCN: 建立中的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: The establishing committee met weekly.
items.exampleCN: 筹建委员会每周开会。

definition_zh: 估计；估算；评价；看法；尊重；（统计）估计值；（成本）估算；（历史）估价；目测
definition_en: the act of calculating an approximate value; a judgment or opinion of someone or something; respect or esteem; (statistics) a value inferred from sample data; a costing prepared in advance; (historical) an official valuation of property

senses.title: A judgment or opinion
senses.definition: a considered opinion about the nature, quality, or value of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人某物的性质、质量或价值经过考虑的看法
senses.example: In my estimation, the plan is too risky to start this year.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这个计划风险太大，今年不宜启动。
senses.why: Estimation is estimate + -ion. Estimate comes from Latin aestimare 'to value, appraise'. The noun therefore begins as a valuation: a mind placing a price or worth on something.
senses.whyCN: estimation 是 estimate + -ion。estimate 来自拉丁语 aestimare“估价、评估”。因此这个名词起点是估值：心智给某物定一个价或价值。

senses.title: An approximate calculation
senses.definition: a calculated guess of an amount, size, or time, usually with some uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 对数量、规模或时间作出的计算性猜测，通常带有不确定性
senses.example: Our estimation of the crowd was about five thousand people.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估计人群约有五千人。
senses.why: This is the everyday quantitative sense: a number produced without exact measurement. Good estimation states its method and its error, which is why engineers write '±10%' beside it.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常定量义：未经精确测量得出的数字。好的估算会说明方法与误差，所以工程师会在旁边写“±10%”。

senses.title: Respect or esteem
senses.definition: the high regard in which a person is held by others
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人的高度评价与敬重
senses.example: She was held in high estimation by her colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 她受到同事们的高度敬重。
senses.why: The 'value' in aestimare can be social worth, not money. This sense survives mainly in formal phrases such as 'held in high estimation', where the verb hold signals a lasting public judgment.
senses.whyCN: aestimare 的“价值”可以是社会价值，而非金钱。这个义项主要存于 held in high estimation 等正式短语中，其中 hold 表示持久的公众判断。

senses.title: A statistical estimate
senses.definition: a value of a population parameter inferred from sample data
senses.definitionCN: 由样本数据推断出的总体参数值
senses.example: The estimation of the mean relied on a small sample.
senses.exampleCN: 对均值的估计依赖一个小样本。
senses.why: Statistics turns the word into a technical object: an estimation procedure produces an estimator, and its quality is judged by bias and variance. The noun can name the method or the resulting number.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把这个词变成技术对象：估计程序产生估计量，其质量由偏差与方差评判。这个名词既可命名方法，也可命名所得数字。

senses.title: A cost estimate
senses.definition: a calculation of the likely cost of a project before it is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 项目执行前对其可能成本的计算
senses.example: The builder's estimation came in below the architect's budget.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商的估算低于建筑师的预算。
senses.why: Business and construction use the word for forward-looking numbers that become commitments. An estimation is softer than a quote: it can be revised when conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 商业与建筑业用这个词指前瞻性数字，而它后来会变成承诺。estimation 比报价软：条件变化时可以修改。

senses.title: An official valuation of property
senses.definition: a formal assessment of the value of property, especially for tax or legal purposes
senses.definitionCN: 对财产价值的正式评估，尤用于税务或法律目的
senses.example: The estate was listed at a high estimation for tax purposes.
senses.exampleCN: 该地产为税务目的被估了很高的价值。
senses.why: Historical and legal usage keeps the oldest sense visible: estimation is what an authority says something is worth. The number is not a guess but an official act with consequences.
senses.whyCN: 历史与法律用法让最古老的义项可见：estimation 是权威宣布某物值多少。这个数字不是猜测，而是有后果的官方行为。

senses.title: Judging distance or size by eye
senses.definition: a judgment of distance, height, or size made without instruments
senses.definitionCN: 不使用仪器对距离、高度或大小作出的判断
senses.example: By estimation, the opposite bank was forty metres away.
senses.exampleCN: 凭目测，对岸大约四十米远。
senses.why: This sense is embodied rather than numerical: the body compares what it sees with what it remembers. The phrase 'by estimation' marks the result as approximate and personal.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是具身的，而非纯数字：身体把所见与所记比较。by estimation 这一说法标记结果为近似且个人化。

senses.title: Population size estimation
senses.definition: the process of inferring the size of a wild population from samples or signs
senses.definitionCN: 由样本或痕迹推断野生种群规模的过程
senses.example: Mark-recapture is a standard method of population estimation.
senses.exampleCN: 标记重捕是种群数量估计的标准方法。
senses.why: Field biology applies the statistical sense to animals that cannot be counted directly. The estimation combines sampling design with assumptions, and its uncertainty is part of the result.
senses.whyCN: 野外生物学把统计义用于无法直接计数的动物。估计把抽样设计与假设结合起来，其不确定性是结果的一部分。

intro.en: Estimation is estimate + -ion. Estimate comes from Latin aestimare 'to value, appraise', whose noun aestimatio meant 'a valuation'. English esteem is a doublet of estimate, which is why 'high estimation' and 'high esteem' mean almost the same thing.
intro.cn: estimation 是 estimate + -ion。estimate 来自拉丁语 aestimare“估价、评估”，其名词 aestimatio 意为“估值”。英语 esteem 是 estimate 的同源双式词，所以 high estimation 与 high esteem 意思几乎相同。

items.en: Latin aestimare meant 'to value, appraise, judge the worth of'. Aestimatio was the noun of action, used for official valuations as well as personal judgments.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为“估价、评估、判断价值”。aestimatio 是动作名词，既用于官方估价，也用于个人判断。

items.en: Old French estimer and estimation carried the Latin words into medieval usage, where estimation often meant an official assessment of property or goods.
items.cn: 古法语 estimer 与 estimation 把拉丁词带入中世纪用法，其中 estimation 常指对财产或货物的官方评估。

items.en: English estimation appears in the fourteenth century with both the 'valuation' and 'opinion' senses. The two have remained intertwined because a valuation is a kind of opinion with a number attached.
items.cn: 英语 estimation 于 14 世纪出现，同时带“估价”与“看法”义。两者一直交织，因为估值就是附了数字的看法。

items.en: The sense 'esteem, high regard' settled in phrases such as 'in high estimation'. The verb esteem developed as a parallel borrowing of the same Latin root.
items.cn: “敬重、高度评价”义固定于 in high estimation 等短语。动词 esteem 作为同一拉丁词根的另一条借入线发展起来。

items.en: Statistical estimation emerged as a technical field: sample data are used to infer population values, and estimators are judged by bias and variance.
items.cn: 统计估计作为技术领域出现：用样本数据推断总体值，估计量按偏差与方差评判。

items.en: Cost and schedule estimation became standard practice in engineering and construction, with explicit uncertainty ranges. The word now often appears next to '±'.
items.cn: 成本与工期估算成为工程与建筑的标准做法，并明确标注不确定范围。这个词如今常与“±”一起出现。

note.en: The first group separates the estimate family from one another; the second group separates estimation from related nouns of calculation and judgment.
note.cn: 第一组区分 estimate 词族内部的关系；第二组区分 estimation 与相邻的“计算”“判断”名词。

entries.definition: an approximate calculation, or to make one. It is the base that -ion nominalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 近似计算，或进行近似计算。它是被 -ion 名词化的底座。

entries.definition: a person who estimates, or a statistical rule for producing estimates. The -or suffix marks the agent or instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 做估算的人，或产生估计值的统计规则。-or 后缀标记施动者或工具。

entries.definition: worthy of respect; also able to be estimated. It splits into a social and a numerical sense, just like the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 值得尊敬的；也可指可估计的。它像名词一样分成社会义与数字义。

entries.definition: a specific approximate figure. It is countable and concrete, while estimation can name the process or the opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 具体的近似数字。它可数而具体，而 estimation 可命名过程或看法。

entries.definition: a formal judgment of quality or performance. It is usually structured and criteria-based, whereas estimation may be informal or numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 对质量或表现的正式判断。它通常有结构、有标准，而 estimation 可以是非正式或数字性的。

entries.definition: the act of deciding monetary worth, especially of property. It overlaps the historical sense of estimation but is now the standard financial word.
entries.definitionCN: 决定货币价值的行为，尤指财产。它与 estimation 的历史义重叠，但如今是标准的财务用词。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Latin aestimare 'value', the doublet estimate / esteem, the phrase in my estimation, and the technical term statistical estimation.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 aestimare“估价”、同源双式词 estimate / esteem、短语 in my estimation，以及专业术语 statistical estimation。

normal.en: aestimare means 'to value': estimation begins as putting a worth on something, not measuring it exactly.
normal.cn: aestimare 意为“估价”：estimation 起点是给某物定价值，而非精确测量。

normal.en: In my estimation is a formal way to say 'in my opinion', because a valuation is a kind of opinion.
normal.cn: in my estimation 是“依我看”的正式说法，因为估值就是一种看法。

normal.en: Estimate + -ion: the verb and noun differ only by the -ion and a stress shift.
normal.cn: estimate + -ion：动词与名词只差 -ion 与重音位置。

normal.en: Statistics separates the estimator (the rule) from the estimate (the number it produces).
normal.cn: 统计学把 estimator（规则）与 estimate（它产生的数字）分开。

normal.en: '±10%' is honest estimation: a number plus its uncertainty.
normal.cn: “±10%”是诚实的估算：一个数字加上它的不确定性。

abstract.en: A valuation is a judgment that has agreed to become a number.
abstract.cn: 估值是一个同意变成数字的判断。

abstract.en: Estimation is how thought behaves under uncertainty: it moves before it has proof, and it says so.
abstract.cn: 估算是在不确定下的思维行为：它在有证据前就行动，并承认这一点。

abstract.en: Every estimate carries the shadow of its error; the shadow is part of the estimate, not a defect in it.
abstract.cn: 每个估计都带着误差的影子；影子是估计的一部分，而非缺陷。

examples.en: In my estimation, the benefits outweigh the risks by a wide margin.
examples.cn: 依我看，收益远远大于风险。

examples.en: The cost estimation was revised after the steel prices rose.
examples.cn: 钢材价格上涨后，成本估算被修订。

examples.en: Population estimation from tracks is less precise than mark-recapture.
examples.cn: 根据痕迹估计种群数量不如标记重捕精确。

dict_mnemonic.text: “estim，门神”——estim 是门口那位神，先估一估来客值多少 → estimation 估计、评价

root: estimate（估计，拉丁语 aestimare“估价”）+ -ion（动作／结果名词后缀）；字面义“作出估值”，核心是“在没有精确测量时给出数字或判断”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of estimation all place a value under uncertainty: an opinion, a rough number, a person's standing, a statistical inference, a project cost, an official valuation, an eye-measured distance, a wildlife count. The word is honest about approximation, and that honesty is what separates it from measurement.
sensesIntro.cn: estimation 的八个义项都在不确定下给出价值：看法、粗略数字、个人声望、统计推断、工程成本、官方估价、目测距离、野生动物计数。这个词对“近似”是诚实的，而这种诚实正是它区别于测量的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number written on a board with a small '±' beside it — a judgment that admits its own error.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上写着一个数字，旁边标着小小的“±”——一个承认自身误差的判断。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: a considered opinion, and the high regard in which a person is held, are both valuations of worth.
branches.cn: 判断：经过考虑的看法，以及他人对某人的高度敬重，都是对价值的评估。

branches.en: APPROXIMATION: a rough number and an eye-measured distance are estimates made without instruments.
branches.cn: 近似：粗略数字与目测距离都是不用仪器作出的估计。

branches.en: PROFESSIONAL: statistical inference and project costing produce numbers with explicit uncertainty.
branches.cn: 专业：统计推断与工程成本产生带明确不确定性的数字。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: an official valuation is an estimate backed by legal consequence.
branches.cn: 权威：官方估价是有法律后果背书的估计。

branches.en: FIELD SCIENCE: a population is inferred from samples, so uncertainty is built into the result.
branches.cn: 野外科学：种群由样本推断，不确定性内建于结果。

intro.en: Estimation is a Latin-derived -ion noun on estimate. The affix set shows the verb/noun pair, the agent noun, the adjective, and the same-root doublet esteem, which took the 'respect' branch.
intro.cn: estimation 是拉丁来源、以 estimate 为基础的 -ion 名词。词缀组展示动词／名词对、施动名词、形容词，以及走“尊重”分支的同源双式词 esteem。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare 'to value' yields aestimatio and, through French, English estimate and esteem. The two English words are doublets: same source, different routes and different modern senses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare“估价”产生 aestimatio，并经法语产生英语 estimate 与 esteem。这两个英语词是同源双式词：同一来源、不同路径、不同现代义。

items.meaning: the act of estimating, or a judgment of worth
items.meaningCN: 估计；评价（-ion 表动作或结果）
items.example: Their estimation of the cost was too low.
items.exampleCN: 他们对成本的估计太低。

items.meaning: to calculate approximately; an approximate figure
items.meaningCN: 估计；估算（动词／名词）
items.example: Engineers estimate the load first.
items.exampleCN: 工程师先估算负载。

items.meaning: one who estimates; a statistical rule
items.meaningCN: 估算者；估计量（-or 表施动者）
items.example: The estimator uses three years of data.
items.exampleCN: 估计量使用三年数据。

items.meaning: worthy of esteem; able to be estimated
items.meaningCN: 值得尊敬的；可估计的（-able 形容词）
items.example: She is an estimable colleague.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位值得尊敬的同事。

items.meaningCN: 尊重；敬重（同源双式词）
items.example: The teacher earned the esteem of her students.
items.exampleCN: 这位老师赢得了学生的敬重。

items.meaningCN: 评估（不同词根，勿混同）
items.example: The assessment took two days.
items.exampleCN: 评估用了两天。

items.meaning: the act of setting a monetary value
items.meaningCN: 估价；估值（value + -ation）
items.example: The valuation of the firm was contested.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的估值受到争议。

items.meaningCN: 高估（over- + estimate）
items.example: We overestimated the demand.
items.exampleCN: 我们高估了需求。
